remote.title: Director, Compliance
remote.description:
About Riot Platforms

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. Riot’s mission is to empower the future of digital infrastructure by positively impacting the sectors, networks, and communities that we touch. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure.

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

The Director, Compliance owns the engine that keeps Riot audit-ready year-round: the controls framework, the testing program, the issues and remediation lifecycle, and the GRC platform that ties all of it together. Compliance designs the controls that prove that policies are working — and builds the automation infrastructure that makes proving it sustainable at scale.

This pillar is intentionally scoped to execute, not to govern or audit. Compliance owns the unified control library — design, mapping to ISO 27001 Annex A, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, NIST CSF, and SOX ITGC — along with owner assignment and testing cadences. Compliance owns the testing program across design adequacy and operating effectiveness. Compliance owns the issues and remediation lifecycle. And Compliance owns the GRC platform: selection, implementation, configuration, integrations, and ongoing administration.

You will report to the Senior Director, GRC and partner directly with IT and Security Engineering as the primary technical counterparts for control evidence, cloud configuration reviews, and platform integrations. In critical operations, you will work with mining site and data center teams to ensure operational controls — physical access, environmental monitoring, asset management — are designed, tested, and evidenced to the same standard as enterprise IT controls.

This role has one non-negotiable: you must be an operator, not just a strategist. In Year 1 you will personally administer the GRC platform, configure the control library, build integrations, and drive the automation that eliminates manual audit prep.

What you'll do

- Design and build the Riot unified controls framework: map the control universe to ISO 27001 Annex A, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, NIST CSF, and SOX ITGC; assign control owners; define testing frequencies; and rationalize overlapping framework requirements into a single, audit-efficient control set.

- Own the ISO 27001:2022 controls implementation track — designing, implementing, and evidencing all Annex A controls required for certification, on a schedule with no buffer.

- Execute the control testing program across all in-scope frameworks: design adequacy and operating effectiveness testing, evidence documentation to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audit-quality standards, and a continuous testing calendar that eliminates point-in-time audit scrambles.

- Lead GRC platform selection, implementation, and administration: evaluate vendors (ServiceNow GRC, Vanta, Drata, Hyperproof, OneTrust, or equivalent), build the business case, drive implementation to production, and own the platform as the system of record for all GRC controls, risks, and evidence.

- Build and operate the issues and remediation lifecycle: intake all control failures and audit findings from across all pillars, assign ownership, track remediation progress, validate closure, and feed status into the POA&M program in coordination with the Director, Risk Management.

- Drive compliance automation: identify manual, spreadsheet-based workflows and replace them with automated evidence collection, integrated dashboards, and real-time controls monitoring — integrating the GRC platform with Asana, identity providers, AWS/Azure, and operational source systems.

- Engage mining site and data center teams to design, implement, test, and evidence operational controls (physical access, environmental monitoring, change management, asset management) to the same standard as enterprise IT controls.

What you'll bring

- 8–12+ years of progressive GRC, IT audit, controls design, or compliance program experience, with hands-on GRC platform administration (required — not observer-level familiarity).

- ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor certification — required. The Director, Compliance owns the controls framework that underpins ISO 27001:2022 certification. A lead-level credential is the baseline, not a preference.

- Demonstrated experience designing a controls framework mapped simultaneously to multiple standards (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, SOX ITGC) and rationalized to a unified, audit-efficient control set.

- Direct experience executing control testing programs: design adequacy and operating effectiveness testing, evidence documentation to audit-quality standards, and reporting testing results to senior leadership.

- Proven GRC platform experience as a power user or administrator — control library configuration, evidence mapping, workflow design, and integration with source systems (Asana, identity providers, AWS/Azure).

- Strong automation and integration mindset: experience building automated evidence pipelines, dashboard reporting, or integrations between GRC platforms and operational systems.

- Experience managing an issues and remediation lifecycle (POA&M): tracking, owner accountability, escalation, and closure validation across cross-functional control owners.

- Technical fluency: comfortable evaluating AWS and Azure security configurations as control evidence; familiarity with API-based GRC integrations; light scripting (Python, SQL) or AI-assisted automation is a strong plus.

- Preferred: CISA certification; experience in critical infrastructure, data center, or digital asset environments; experience with SOC 2 evidence preparation and auditor walkthrough facilitation.

Compensation and Benefits

- Competitive Salary: Base range (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant.

- Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build.

- 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match.

- Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans.

- Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Objetivo do cargo
O(a) Especialista de Inteligência de Mercado será responsável por transformar dados internos e externos em inteligência estratégica para apoiar decisões comerciais e de negócio.
Atuará na identificação de tendências, oportunidades e riscos de mercado, combinando informações de mercado, concorrência, clientes, canais, categorias e performance interna, com o objetivo de orientar decisões de crescimento, priorização de oportunidades e estratégia de Go-to-Market.
Será referência técnica em Inteligência de Mercado, sendo responsável por desenvolver análises de maior complexidade, estruturar metodologias e traduzir informações em recomendações acionáveis para a liderança e áreas comerciais.
Principais responsabilidades Inteligência de Mercado e Concorrência

- Monitorar continuamente o mercado, identificando tendências, mudanças de comportamento, oportunidades e riscos para o negócio.

- Analisar movimentos dos principais concorrentes, incluindo posicionamento, portfólio, preços, canais, lançamentos e estratégias comerciais.

- Estruturar estudos de mercado para dimensionamento de categorias, segmentos, regiões e canais.

- Desenvolver análises de Wallet Share, Market Share e potencial de mercado.

- Construir cenários e análises que auxiliem a companhia a antecipar movimentos de mercado.

- Identificar espaços de crescimento e oportunidades ainda pouco exploradas pela organização.

Clientes, Segmentação e Potencial

- Desenvolver estudos de segmentação e potencial de clientes, mercados e territórios.

- Identificar perfis e clusters de clientes com maior potencial de crescimento.

- Analisar comportamento de compra, frequência, mix, penetração e evolução dos clientes.

- Apoiar a definição e evolução do ICP (Ideal Customer Profile) e dos critérios de priorização comercial.

- Identificar oportunidades de aquisição, retenção, cross-sell e expansão da base de clientes.

- Apoiar análises de potencial e cobertura comercial.

Suporte à Estratégia de GTM

- Fornecer inteligência de mercado para construção e revisão das estratégias de Go-to-Market.

- Apoiar decisões sobre onde jogar e como ganhar, indicando mercados, segmentos, clientes, canais e categorias prioritárias.

- Conectar informações externas de mercado com dados internos de performance comercial.

- Apoiar estudos para entrada em novos mercados, regiões, canais ou segmentos.

- Avaliar oportunidades de crescimento e estimar seu potencial financeiro e comercial.

- Trabalhar em parceria com Sales Operations, Marketing, Comercial e demais áreas na construção de recomendações estratégicas.

Análises Estratégicas e Geração de Insights

- Desenvolver análises avançadas que expliquem não apenas o que aconteceu, mas principalmente por que aconteceu e quais ações devem ser tomadas.

- Identificar drivers de crescimento, perda de performance e mudanças relevantes no mercado.

- Desenvolver business cases para avaliação de oportunidades.

- Construir cenários, projeções e análises de sensibilidade.

- Traduzir análises complexas em recomendações claras e objetivas para diferentes públicos.

- Preparar materiais executivos para fóruns de decisão e reuniões de liderança.

- Garantir consistência e qualidade das informações utilizadas nos estudos de mercado.

- Integrar diferentes fontes de dados para construir uma visão única do mercado.

- Desenvolver metodologias e padrões para análises recorrentes de Inteligência de Mercado.

- Apoiar a automatização e evolução das análises e indicadores da área.

- Dimensionamento de mercado (Market Size)

- Análises de Market Share

- Mapas de oportunidades

- Estudos de potencial por cliente, região, canal ou segmento

- Segmentação e clusterização de clientes

- Análises de tendências

- Monitoramento competitivo

- Estudos de entrada em novos mercados

- Business cases

- Cenários e projeções de mercado

- Recomendações para estratégias de GTM

- Apresentações executivas e recomendações para a liderança

- PMM

- Parcerias

- Dados / BI

- Acuracidade das projeções e estimativas de mercado

- Qualidade e confiabilidade dos estudos

- Utilização das análises nas decisões de negócio

- Oportunidades de crescimento identificadas

- Evolução do Market Share nos mercados priorizados

- Assertividade das segmentações e modelos de potencial

- Adoção das recomendações pelas áreas de negócio

- SLA e qualidade das entregas estratégicas

Qualifications

- Orientação para resultados

- Pensamento estratégico

- Capacidade de conectar diferentes fontes de informação

- Forte capacidade analítica

- Visão de negócio e mercado

- Comunicação e influência

remote.description:
Scope of Work

- Review DGE's existing "TranslationHub" inventory (user type, feature, category, description) and the comprehensive Figma user-journey document, and use them as the source material for course scoping.

- Break down features and processes into course modules, grouped by workflow ("flow") and by persona, using logical/module-based grouping rather than a strict feature-by-feature structure.

- Design and build storyboards for each course (in Figma or PowerPoint, per DGE's internal decision).

- Develop each course as an interactive Articulate course, including:

- An introduction/welcome segment

- A conversational Q&A segment that sets the baseline objective

- A guided, step-by-step process simulation

- A graded assessment

- Write the two-person conversational scripts used for each course's intro/Q&A segment for AI voiceover generation.

- Build guided, click-through process simulations that mimic the live TranslationHub platform screens end to end.

- Write MCQ-based question banks for each course's assessment.

- Package finished courses as SCORM-compliant files and hand them over to the CDP platform team for upload. The freelancer/DGE side will not have production upload access.

- Coordinate with Hashem Adnan Jadan on Arabic localization, terminology alignment, and course QA sign-off.

- Participate in recurring weekly syncs with the CDP platform team, as well as a technical kickoff/recap call early in the engagement.

Required Skills & Tools
Mandatory

- Proven, hands-on experience with Articulate (Storyline or equivalent). This is the client's licensed, standard authoring tool, so candidates must already have experience using it.

- Experience packaging and delivering SCORM-compliant e-learning courses.

- Instructional design experience for enterprise, process, or system training, particularly software walkthroughs and role-based workflows rather than general knowledge courses.

- Comfortable designing from a Figma or PowerPoint storyboard and building guided platform simulations (click-through, step-by-step process walkthroughs).

- Experience designing course assessments, including MCQ question banks, pass thresholds, and section-based question pools.

Preferred / Nice to Have

- Experience with AI voiceover tools (the client's platform team uses ElevenLabs) and writing conversational, two-presenter scripts for voiceover generation.

- Arabic-language e-learning localization experience, particularly Modern Standard/official Arabic rather than colloquial dialects.

- Prior experience building courses for a government or public-sector ERP/HR platform, or a similar large-scale enterprise rollout.

remote.description:
Our vision for the future is based on the idea that transforming financial lives starts by giving our people the freedom to transform their own. We have a flexible work environment, and fluid career paths. We not only encourage but celebrate internal mobility. We also recognize the importance of purpose, well-being, and work-life balance. The Sr Manager Data Products & Strategy will lead the execution and ongoing management of data products within assigned data domains or areas of the organization. This role manages teams responsible for delivering governed, reusable, and high-value data products that enable critical business decisions within a highly regulated financial services environment. The Sr Manager partners closely with Technology, Analytics, Data Governance, Risk, Compliance, and Business stakeholders to translate data priorities into actionable product plans, coordinate delivery across teams, and ensure data products meet established business, quality, and regulatory requirements. This role also provides input into broader data product strategy while maintaining accountability for the performance, priorities, and results of assigned teams.
What you will do:

- Provide input into data product strategy, standards, and objectives for assigned data domains or product areas, and translate broader data strategy and priorities into actionable product plans, roadmaps, and team deliverables.

- Manage assigned data product portfolios, which may include advisor, customer, accounts, risk, operations, or other data domains.

- Prioritize product initiatives based on business value, stakeholder needs, dependencies, risk, and available resources.

- Adapt departmental plans and resources to address changing business priorities and delivery challenges.

- Ensure product plans have clearly defined objectives, requirements, measures of success, and expected business outcomes.

- Lead and manage a team of Data Product Managers and/or other professional-level employees.

- Establish team priorities and ensure alignment with department and broader data product objectives.

- Provide coaching, performance management, development, and ongoing guidance to direct reports.

- Promote consistent practices for product discovery, requirements definition, documentation, prioritization, and delivery.

- Build team capabilities and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement.

- Make or recommend staffing and other personnel decisions in accordance with organizational policies.

- Manage delivery of complex data products and initiatives within assigned domains or areas of responsibility.

- Coordinate across data product, data engineering, analytics, technology, and business teams to achieve department objectives.

- Identify and resolve delivery issues, resource constraints, dependencies, and competing priorities within assigned areas.

- Escalate significant cross-functional risks or issues to department or sub-functional leadership when appropriate.

- Monitor team execution against product roadmaps, milestones, service expectations, and established measures.

- Ensure teams apply established product management practices and operating standards consistently.

- Partner with Data Governance, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Security, Privacy, and Technology teams to implement required controls within assigned data products.

- Ensure assigned data products comply with established requirements for privacy, data quality, lineage, auditability, retention, access, and other applicable controls.

- Implement established data ownership, stewardship, and accountability practices within assigned domains.

- Identify and escalate material data risks and support timely remediation.

- Ensure product requirements appropriately incorporate regulatory, governance, and risk considerations throughout the product lifecycle.

- Develop productive relationships with business, technology, analytics, risk, compliance, and data stakeholders.

- Partner with stakeholders to understand business needs, establish priorities, and translate requirements into data product outcomes.

- Communicate product roadmaps, delivery progress, risks, dependencies, and value realization to department and sub-functional leadership.

- Monitor product performance and identify opportunities to improve existing data products, processes, and services.

- Support business case development and track expected benefits and value realization for assigned initiatives.

- Use product performance, stakeholder feedback, and business priorities to recommend changes to product plans and roadmaps.

- 4 year degree or equivalent experience.

- 8+ years of relevant experience in product management, data, analytics, technology, or related disciplines, including significant experience with data, analytics, or platform products.

- Strong understanding of enterprise data platforms and modern data architectures, including data lakes, data warehouses, and/or streaming technologies.

- Understanding of analytics, business intelligence, metrics, and related data consumption patterns.

- Experience with data governance practices, including metadata management, data lineage, data quality, privacy, and data controls.

- Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional data or technology initiatives.

- Ability to translate broader strategic priorities into actionable product plans and team deliverables.

- Strong stakeholder management, communication, prioritization, and problem-solving skills.

- Experience with cloud-native data ecosystems such as AWS, Snowflake, or Redshift.

- Familiarity with data mesh, domain-oriented data product models, or similar modern data management practices.

- Background in product management, analytics, engineering, data, or quantitative disciplines.

- Experience preparing and presenting product information to senior leadership and governance forums.

remote.title: Applied AI Security Engineer
remote.description:
Waabi, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we're unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that's powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech.
With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit:

Waabi is leaning into an AI-native strategy — not just in our trucks, but in how we build, ship, and operate every day. Our teams leverage key AI tools to enhance productivity and efficiency, continuously expanding AI integration across our systems and workflows. That's a huge unlock, and it's moving fast. We're looking for someone to make sure it keeps moving fast safely — by establishing the guardrails and collaborating on the implementation of sandboxes and automations that let people adopt AI with confidence instead of second-guessing themselves. You'll join a small, sharp security team and take primary ownership of AI security controls and considerations across the company. If you've got a developer's instincts, a security mindset, and you're genuinely curious about what these tools can and can't be trusted to do, this role is built around you.
You will...

- Audit how AI tools and MCP integrations are currently used across the company, and map where they touch sensitive systems, data, or credentials for the purpose of defining policy.

- Design and implement layered guardrails - enterprise-level system prompts, scoped permissions, sandboxing patterns - that constrain AI behavior before it ever reaches a user's request.

- Maintain an inventory of both MCP servers and AI-to-service connections and their data access controls, with a clear model of what each one can access and why.

- Partner directly with users across the organization to bake secure-by-default patterns into their AI-assisted workflows so that written policy doesn’t just sit on a shelf.

- Evaluate new AI tools, plugins, and integration requests, and figure out the secure way to say yes.

- Continuously test and red-team your own guardrails - assume they'll be pushed on, and find the gaps before someone else does.

- Document guidance and patterns that a non-security audience can actually follow without needing a security background.

Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.

- Professional software development experience, with solid fundamentals in how services, APIs, and permissions fit together.

- Hands-on experience using AI coding/productivity tools (Claude, Copilot, Gemini, or similar) in business-critical workflows.

- Working knowledge of core security concepts — least privilege, sandboxing, trust boundaries, threat modeling basics.

- Strong communication skills - you work with engineers as a partner.

Bonus:

- Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or similar tool-calling/agent-integration frameworks.

- Exposure to prompt injection, jailbreaking, or other AI/LLM-specific attack techniques.

- Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or other safety-critical systems

The SHI Services Solutions Engineer, Data Engineering is a key contributor within our Microsoft Data and AI practice. This role is responsible for designing, building, and delivering enterprise scale data engineering solutions using the Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Fabric ecosystems. The Solutions Engineer works closely with Solution Engineers, Principal Engineers, Project Managers, and client stakeholders to implement secure, scalable, and compliant data platforms and pipelines that support analytics, reporting, and AI driven use cases.

This role is hands on and delivery focused. Associate Solutions Engineers are expected to execute technical designs, own discrete data engineering workstreams, and contribute directly to successful client outcomes. This role reflects SHI’s commitment to delivering enterprise-grade data platforms that power analytics, insights, and AI at scale. - Design, develop, and implement data ingestion, transformation, and integration pipelines using Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics, Microsoft Fabric, and related Azure data services

- Build and optimize data lakehouse and warehouse solutions in Azure and Microsoft Fabric, ensuring scalability, reliability, security, and cost effectiveness

- Implement monitoring and operational reporting for pipelines and data platforms to support production support models

- Demonstrate ownership and accountability for assigned deliverables and proactively address delivery risks

The Implementation Engineer is a customer-facing, billable position chartered with engaging customers in a consultative capacity and providing specialized expertise around NiCE products the contact center industry, and other contact center ecosystem topics including CRM, telecommunications infrastructure, analytics, social media, and others.

This position, depending on the types of projects onto which he or she is deployed, will be responsible for both technical and business tasks including managing customer expectations and satisfaction, configuring NiCE products based on best practices and customer requirements, coordinating inter-departmental activities within NiCE, tracking time and status within NiCE systems, and other tasks related to the success of his or her engagement.

The Implementation Engineer is also an organizational leader and is expected to serve as a mentor and coach for junior staff.

​This position is responsible for consultative performance in all areas related to NiCE solutions provisioning, implementation, and deployment of technical and business solutions to clients. The customer base consists of public and private sector agencies and businesses employing diverse information management and contact center environments.

As a Implementation Engineer, a Typical Day Might Include the Following:

TECHNICAL

- Provide technical configuration and, in some cases, programming as required.

- Provide process, data and object modeling in a variety of application and database environments.

- Provide database design, development, and enhancement, as well as management and coordination of changes to existing applications.

- Provide technical architecture leadership, analysis, design, development, and enhancement.

- Maintain expertise and currency in industry leading contact center technologies.
PROJECT

- Serve in a project manager capacity via management of end to end system life cycle development of small to large-scale projects.

- Provide business analysis, business area assessment, user needs analysis and business systems design for major projects.

BUSINESS

- Present a professional image in conduct, attitude and attire.

- Assist with the development of client information management standards and evaluation of technology trends.

- Contribute to business area assessment, user needs analysis and business systems design.

SUPERVISORY

- Supervise during project life cycle any junior level client staff, or any sub-contracted personnel assigned to your project team.
To Land This Gig You'll Need:

- BS/BA in technical (e.g., CS/IS/EE) or business (e.g., Marketing/MIS) field or equivalent work experience required.

- MBA preferred.

- 5+ years of professional experience beyond education requirements above.

- Type of experience varies depending on Professional Service Engineers specialization:

- Implementation: broad skills in both technology & analysis; experience in communicating at a technical and functional level while managing business rapport.

- Business Optimization: deep skills around business analysis/call centers; experience in the KPIs and best practices of call centers and their operations.

- Education & Enablement: professional and confident public presence; experience in commanding large audiences as a trainer and/or speaker.

- Engineering Services: deep skills in specialized technical & functional areas; deeply technical expertise around software engineering, programming languages, integration, and/or databases.

- Desired personal profile: analytical, inquisitive, service & team-oriented, friendly demeanor, early adopter.

- ​Prior consulting experience.

NICE Ltd. remote.title: Senior Security Solutions Engineer
remote.description:
Ever been the person everyone Slacks who either has the answer, or knows how to track it down? That’s this job. As a Senior Security Solutions Engineer, you’re the technical brain trust behind Expel’s Customer Success team — the “the buck stops here” expert who makes sure our CSMs, TAMs, and support engineers always have a fast, accurate answer to bring to customers.
When a customer question gets thorny, it lands with you. You untangle it, you document it so it’s answered even faster next time, and you keep the rest of Expel focused on the work only they can do. If you love being deep in security tech and equally love making other people better at their jobs, keep reading.
What Expel can do for you

- Give you broad exposure to the technology, architecture, integrations, and security operations behind an MDR platform

- Put you close to customers and the technical problems security teams are solving every day

- Give you the opportunity to become a trusted technical resource across Customer Success, Security, Detection & Response, and Engineering

- Let you solve complex technical problems while also building documentation and processes that make the entire organization more effective

- Surround you with curious security practitioners who genuinely enjoy sharing what they know

- Give you room to mentor others, sharpen your own technical depth, and continuously improve how we support our customers

What you can do for Expel

- Be the go-to escalation point for CS — responding quickly and accurately to ad-hoc technical questions from CSMs, TAMs, and TSEs so no one’s left waiting.

- Hop on customer calls when the moment calls for deep technical expertise, backing up the CSM or TAM who owns the relationship.

- Hunt down knowledge gaps and turn them into great documentation — authoring, reviewing, and continuously sharpening technical and process content.

- Partner with teams across Security, Detection & Response, and Engineering to pull knowledge into the team and operationalize it.

- Curate internal and external knowledge repositories and point people to self-service answers when that’s the faster path.

- Enable other teams — especially CSM, TAM, and Technical Support — so the flood of inbound questions gets smaller over time.

- Coach and mentor less experienced teammates, and keep clean records of inquiry volume so the team can prioritize what matters.

What you should bring with you
You’ve spent 7+ years in security, at least half of it in a technical, customer-facing role — ideally consultative. You’ve got real depth across three or more security product spaces (EDR, NDR, SIEM, cloud, you name it) and you can reason about the tradeoffs teams make in security operations. Just as important: you’re a genuinely good communicator who can shift from talking shop with a practitioner to briefing a customer’s senior leadership without missing a beat.
You’ll thrive here if you bring:

- Sharp root-cause analysis and troubleshooting — you diagnose complex technical issues completely and accurately.

- A firm grasp of the cybersecurity market: the products, the providers, and their real strengths and weaknesses.

- Fluency in security controls across Windows, Unix/Linux, AWS, GSuite, O365, and network gear.

- A solid handle on attack vectors, threat tactics, attacker techniques (think ATT&CK), and the attack lifecycle.

- Strong consultative instincts — active listening, conflict management, negotiation, and knowing when (and how gracefully) to escalate.

- An intrinsic drive to self-assess and keep getting better.

A bachelor’s degree and/or relevant certifications are a plus, but we care more about what you can do than where you learned it.
Additional notes
The base salary range for this role is between $122,400 USD and $177,500 USD + variable eligibility and equity. While the full salary band reflects our long-term compensation framework, we're primarily targeting candidates between $145,000 and $165,000 based on experience, skills, and market data.
You’ll also be eligible for unlimited PTO (which we model and encourage), work location flexibility, up to 24 weeks of parental leave, and really excellent health benefits.
We’re only hiring those authorized to work in the United States. We do not currently sponsor immigration visas.
We're an Equal Opportunity Employer: You'll receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.
We’ll ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. This part-time remote opportunity is ideal for technical professionals with hands-on experience in web scraping, data extraction and processing.
What We Do
The Mindrift platform connects specialists with innovative technology projects. Our mission is to help develop high-quality AI technologies by combining real-world expertise from professionals across the globe with advanced AI development efforts.
About the Role
This is a freelance role for a Tendem project. - Own end-to-end data extraction workflows across complex websites, ensuring complete coverage, accuracy, and reliable delivery of structured datasets.

- Leverage available tools and custom workflows to accelerate data collection, validation, and task execution while meeting defined requirement.

- Ensure reliable extraction from dynamic and interactive web sources, adapting approaches as needed to handle JavaScript-rendered content and changing site behavior.

- Enforce data quality standards through validation checks, cross-source consistency controls, adherence to formatting specifications, and systematic verification prior to delivery.

- Scale scraping operations for large datasets using efficient batching or parallelization, monitor failures, and maintain stability against minor site structure changes.

Educational qualifications

Candidates should have a strong technical foundation and practical experience with scripting, automation, and data extraction workflows. - Proven ability to extract data from complex structures (hierarchies, archived pages, inconsistent HTML)

- Solid background in data cleaning, normalization, and validation, delivering structured datasets (CSV, JSON, Google Sheets)

Additional requirements

- Demonstrated experience handling anti-bot mechanisms and dynamic site structures at scale

- Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or equivalent) and containerization (Docker) as part of real workflows

- Hands-on experience with LLM frameworks (LangChain, OpenRouter, or similar) applied to automation tasks

- Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy

- Self-directed work ethic with ability to troubleshoot independently

- A link to GitHub is a plus

- English proficiency: Upper-intermediate (B2) or above (required)

remote.title: Remote Executive Assistant - Business Operations & BD Support
remote.description:
FreedUp is seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Executive Assistant (EA) to support the Founder of a remote-first company building innovative geospatial and open-source software systems. This role is ideal for someone who thrives on structure, accountability, and operational clarity — a professional who can turn complex processes into seamless execution without needing heavy hand-holding.
We're looking for a proactive, detail-oriented Executive Assistant to directly support the Founder — helping streamline both business operations and day-to-day logistics so they can stay focused on building and growing the company. Because the team is fully remote and distributed, this EA needs to be comfortable operating async, communicating clearly in writing, and managing priorities independently.
Above all, the Founder is looking for consistency and proactive follow-through. She'd rather have someone who handles a recurring task the same way every time and reports back without being asked, than someone who is occasionally brilliant but unpredictable.
Location: Fully Remote Job Type:
Full-Time Salary: $1,000 - $1,800 per month (based on experience)
Requirements

- 3+ years of experience as an Executive Assistant, Operations Coordinator, or similar role supporting senior leadership, ideally in a technical or startup environment.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills — with a track record of proactive, consistent communication rather than waiting to be asked for updates.

- Tech-savvy and comfortable working in digital ecosystems (Slack, Gmail, Google Workspace, CRM/project management tools). Comfortable learning new tools independently and setting up better ways of working with them (e.g., automations), rather than expecting mastery to be handed to you.

- Strong organizational and prioritization abilities — able to work independently in an async, distributed team.

- Proven ability to manage sensitive information with sound judgment about who should see what, not just tool-level confidentiality.

- Proactive, self-directed, and thrives in an environment with evolving needs; comfortable operating with minimal oversight.

- Reliable when it comes to calendar commitments — once something is confirmed, it's honored; changes are communicated and explained rather than simply missed.

- Comfortable owning deadlines proactively — including spotting dates buried inside documents (like a procurement RFP) rather than waiting for them to be called out.

- Experience supporting business development, CRM upkeep, or sales pipeline coordination is a plus.

- Experience coordinating (not necessarily authoring) proposals or bid documents is a plus.

- Basic knowledge of expense reporting, reconciliation, or bookkeeping preferred.

-
Technical Requirements: Reliable high-speed internet and a modern home office setup.

Strong Differentiators (not required, but a plus)

- Prior experience supporting an executive or leadership team, especially exposure to how executive meeting agendas are structured — useful as the Founder restructures her own this quarter.

- Comfortable giving and receiving direct feedback — willing to flag it if asked to take on too much, or if something was quietly handled solo after being delegated, rather than just executing silently.

Nice to Haves

- Comfortable navigating dense procurement documents (e.g., project-managing a 100+ page RFP — extracting pricing instructions, page counts, and formatting rules scattered across the document and its amendments).

- Openness to eventually taking on full email/inbox triage once a high-trust working relationship is established (not expected at launch).

- Basic comfort with technical writing (e.g., drafting a short passage on a technical topic like an API) — a bonus, not an expectation.

Key Responsibilities

-
Inbox & Communications Management: Maintain Inbox Zero across email and calls/texts. Triage and respond on behalf of the Founder where appropriate, flag priorities, and keep communications moving without letting things fall through the cracks.

-
Calendar Management & Time Protection: Own and optimize the Founder's calendar, protecting focus time, coordinating meeting scheduling, and confirming, preparing, and taking notes for meetings. Once a meeting is confirmed, it's treated as a firm commitment — no missed RSVPs.

-
Business Development Admin & CRM Upkeep: Maintain and update the CRM and BD pipeline, support prospecting of potential clients, and track business development activity end to end.

-
Proposal & Bid Coordination: Coordinate the preparation of proposals and bids (including government bids covering technical and policy topics), managing timelines, formatting, and inputs from relevant contributors — including proactively surfacing deadlines that are buried in the source documents rather than clearly stated.

Pre-screen the high volume of event/conference invites that come in, flag genuine conflicts (e.g., "you've got three events in two weeks — we think this one, want me to book it?"), and apply the Founder's known personal preferences without needing to ask each time.

-
Expense Reporting & Reconciliation: Handle recurring expense reporting and reconciliation processes, keeping records accurate and organized.

-
Conference Research & Coordination: Research relevant industry conferences and coordinate attendance logistics.

-
Internal Communications & Team Coordination: Serve as a communication link between the Founder and the internal team, keeping updates clear and timely across channels.

Personal & Life Admin Support: Manage doctor appointment scheduling and other personal logistics as needed.

Reporting: Compile a company scorecard and provide structured, proactive updates on priorities, progress, and deadlines — without being asked.

Social Media: Support publishing of social media content as needed.

Event Planning (future scope): Support event planning and coordination as this responsibility area develops.

- Learning and development opportunities

remote.description:
Lyntris is a defense technology company that connects sensing to action across the connected battlespace. Lyntris brings together the talents of Accelint and Vitesse teams under one mission, with each contributing deep expertise within their domain. Combining differentiated hardware, software and mission expertise, Lyntris helps customers sense threats, make sense of complex conditions and act with greater speed, precision and confidence in contested environments.

Lyntris supports U.S. and allied defense organizations across every branch — including Navy, Army, Air Force, Space Force and allied partners — spanning strategic, operational and tactical missions and every domain: Space, Air, Land, Sea and Cyber. With more than 200 active defense programs, Lyntris works at every level of the mission, from national command authority to the tactical edge.

Solutions are designed by operators who understand the mission, engineered for the conditions that degrade or defeat standard systems, and built on an open, modular architecture that integrates into existing programs without requiring them to start over. Lyntris moves faster than the traditional defense cycle — with integrated design, build and test capabilities in-house — and delivers systems that sustain and endure long after initial fielding.

As a Subject Matter Expert (SME), you will design and develop Navy-focused Interactive Multimedia Instruction (IMI) that supports fleet-ready training aligned to NAVEDTRA standards. You will collaborate with highly skilled delivery teams made up of ISDs, Software Engineers, 3D Artists, Graphic Designers, and Technical Leads to analyze, design, develop, test, and deliver Navy training products — and have a great time doing meaningful work that directly supports the warfighter.

Our ideal SME contributes to every phase of the instructional systems design process, validating design decisions with Creative Leadership, the Program Team, and other contributors throughout development. You will ensure accurate implementation of learning objectives, assessments, scenarios, and media elements within Captivate-based IMI, Unity-based simulations, and related digital training solutions.

Our ideal candidate actively participates in weekly design reviews, collaborates with the Creative Operations team, and works closely with engineering and art teams to ensure instructional intent is realized in the final product.

Duties and Responsibilities:

- Conduct front-end analysis, including task analysis, gap analysis, learner analysis, and content reviews based on Navy operational requirements.

- Develop learning objectives, storyboards, scripts, branching scenarios, assessments, and IMI design specifications following NAVEDTRA guidelines.

- Transform complex technical information, manuals into clear, instructionally sound digital learning content.

- Assist Instructional Designers design, structure, and sequence IMI modules delivered through Captivate, Unity, or other training pipelines.

- Collaborate with Software Engineers, Graphic Designers, and 3D Artists to ensure instructional design is accurately implemented in the final product.

- Develop mockups, flowcharts, and prototypes to communicate instructional concepts to stakeholders.

- Ensure alignment with Navy training standards, course control documents (CCDs), TLO/ELO frameworks, and SCORM/xAPI requirements.

- Participate in design reviews with Creative Leadership, Program Managers, and Navy customer stakeholders.

- Evaluate IMI effectiveness and recommend improvements based on learner data, SME feedback, and usability principles.

- Apply design thinking, questioning techniques, and performance-based instructional strategies where pathways may not be fully defined.

- Ensure training products meet accessibility, usability, and quality standards during development and testing.

- Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

- Associate’s Degree. Additional years of relevant experience may substitute for a degree.

- Understanding of instructional design methodologies (ADDIE, SAM, task-based analysis, scenario-based learning).

- Ability to interpret and apply NAVEDTRA standards and Navy training system requirements.

- Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex concepts into clear instructional strategies.

- Ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to implement instructional content.

- Excellent organization, attention to detail, and time-management skills.

- Ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Defense (DOD) Security Clearance.

Preferred Skills (Not Required):

- Experience developing or supporting Navy or DoD training programs.

- Experience in the USN serving as a FC, ET, AT, IC, or any other DoD Service Branch/USN Rating with a thorough background in electronics.

- Familiarity with SCORM, xAPI, and Navy Learning Management Systems.

- Experience working with software engineers or art teams in multimedia development.

- Understanding of accessibility standards and user experience principles in digital training.

- Working knowledge of Adobe Captivate, Unity, Storyline, XD, or related design tools.

- Experience writing or reviewing learning assessments aligned to performance outcomes.

- Familiarity with TLO/ELO alignment, CCDs, and Navy courseware development processes.

Physical Requirements:

- Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

- Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

Positions that require this access will be required to receive and maintain a U.S. government personnel security clearance (PCL). In order to qualify for this position, the candidate must be a US Citizen and either currently possess this National Security eligibility or be able to complete the investigation application process with a favorable determination and maintain that eligibility throughout their employment. remote.title: Salesforce Solutions Architect
remote.description:
Salesforce Solution Architect
Phoenix Team | Remote (U.S.-based) | Full-Time
Overview
The Salesforce Solution Architect supports projects that define requirements and technical solutions for standing up and enhancing Salesforce environments in support of coordinated, multi-product release and regression testing. This role owns the Salesforce side of the solution design — solution architecture, metadata configuration, sandbox strategy, and integration design — spanning both declarative and programmatic (Apex and Lightning Components) Salesforce customization.
The Salesforce Solution Architect works as part of a team to define requirements, produce solution designs, and establish the operating model needed to bring new or updated environments online. Typical activities include determining sandbox type and sizing; defining metadata configuration and environment refresh approaches; sequencing onboarding of in-scope product groups; evaluating and recommending Salesforce integration approaches; and applying Salesforce data sharing and visibility models to the solution design.
The Salesforce Solution Architect will participate in technical discovery sessions with product, testing, and infrastructure stakeholders. Success in this role requires strong, hands-on Salesforce expertise — the ability to work across both flows/configuration and code — along with the ability to take a holistic view of a project's full scope and translate requirements into a solution design that aligns with VA governance, security, and federal compliance standards.
Key Functions

- Produce the solution design for the Salesforce (and, in coordination with the team, AWS) components of the environment.

- Determine sandbox type and sizing needed to support regression testing and performance testing requirements.

- Define the metadata configuration approach for the environment.

- Define the Salesforce refresh approach through the VA Salesforce governance group (DTC), including how refresh requests against production are structured and executed.

- Define the onboarding sequence for product groups being brought into a shared environment.

- Serve as the technical interface with DTC on sandbox provisioning and sandbox control.

- Support determination of the environment's designation and naming, and how it fits within the broader Salesforce Org.

- Support determination of the sandbox control model, including whether the environment operates under program control or DTC control.

- Confirm the test data approach for the environment and the restrictions that apply, including data representativeness, use of production data, and PII handling.

- Design Salesforce integration approaches for the environment, evaluating the available integration patterns and recommending the appropriate approach for each interface.

- Apply Salesforce data sharing and visibility models appropriately within the environment design.

- Troubleshoot Salesforce performance issues and metadata conflicts, and resolve them as part of the solution design.

- Support development of Salesforce test data factories and updates to automated test cases needed to support the environment.

- Take a holistic view of the full scope of the effort, including downstream and cross-product impacts, when designing new sandbox functionality.

remote.title: Group Director Core
remote.description:
Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

**We support 100% remote, in-office, or hybrid work styles for anyone legally eligible to work in the U.S.
A day in the life:
The Group Director, Core is Power Digital's senior client relationship and revenue leader for a portfolio of primarily small business, founder-led clients. Your clients are often making their first serious investment in outside marketing help — the founder is usually the client, the budget is real money out of their own pocket, and a single underperforming month can feel existential in a way it rarely does at the enterprise level. You manage a higher-volume portfolio than almost any other Group Director role, and you run it the way a disciplined fund manager runs a broad, diversified book: fewer swings for the fences on any single account, more rigor in the system that keeps every account healthy. You are the executive a founder calls directly — there's no committee and no VP layer between you and the person who built the business — and the leader an Account Director never wants to let down. The roles you consistently play day-to-day are: portfolio growth owner, talent multiplier, tech forward leader and AI systems thinker.
At Power, retention is the floor, not the job. You are commercially driven first: you personally own executive relationships and expansion revenue for the top of your portfolio, and you hold your team to the same standard. In Core, that means running a scalable, standardized system — foundational packages, repeatable playbooks, and efficient triage — rather than bespoke strategy for every account, because the portfolio is wider and the margin for one-off customization is thinner than at any other tier. You coach Account Directors and their teams to operate as AI-Native Growth Directors — faster, sharper, and less buried in manual work than the role has ever required before. You decide which AI tools and workflows the division adopts. Your influence runs beyond Client Experience: you shape your Division's go-to-market position, you're a thought partner to your Managing Director and VP, and you represent Power Digital in market on how small, founder-led businesses can grow with limited resources.
Key Responsibilities:

- Own net revenue retention and expansion MRR for the division; treat expansion as the primary commercial lever of the role and own the division's monthly service expansion target

- Personally own executive relationships across the top 10-20% of the portfolio by MRR — direct relationship, not delegated

- Run quarterly, relationship-focused executive check-ins with top-tier accounts and 1x1 check-ins with every priority account

- Maintain an accurate, self-owned retention forecast on a weekly basis — accountable for the accuracy of the division's retention data

- Track vertical-specific signal such as founder engagement and responsiveness, service package utilization, and time-to-first-win on foundational packages, since a disengaged founder or a stalled quick win is often the earliest warning sign of churn at this tier

- Diagnose risk early and install fixes, not just responses; lead or co-lead quarterly plans for the top 10% of the portfolio, weighted toward strategic outcomes over metrics recaps

- Partner with Account Directors to build value-based, consultative business cases — expansion should drive value, not be sold

- Identify and lead common Core expansion paths, including upsell from foundational packages into additional service lines, and efficient, template-driven expansion offers built for speed rather than custom-built proposals

- Work with Account Directors to keep the Salesforce pipeline current and accurate — stages, forecast, and next steps updated weekly

- Serve as the frontline for product and vertical innovation, feeding client signal into Power Circuit

- Build and evolve vertical-relevant reporting frameworks for Core, including metrics such as time-to-first-win, founder engagement/response rate, and package-level utilization, built to work at scale across a high-volume portfolio

- Play a key leadership role in final-round pitches for prospective clients where support is needed

- Bring vertical point of view and executive credibility to new business

- Partner with Sales to sharpen positioning, collateral, and win rate for the division's go-to-market

- Directly manage Account Directors and oversee the pod that supports them

- Coach every direct report to operate as an AI-Native Growth Director, not a task manager — faster diagnosis, more client-facing time, less manual reporting

- Evaluate the team on Pulse sentiment, health scores, and expansion weekly — not just activity

- Raise the floor on AI adoption — no one on the team operates the old way

- Own hiring, staffing, capacity, and career pathing for the division; facilitate DAPs and career progression conversations

- Practice radical candor; deliver timely, actionable feedback that accelerates careers

- Identify and develop key talent for future Sr. Account Director & Group Director roles

- Lead training on vertical-specific and AI-native tools, processes, and strategies

- Vibe-codes prototypes to automate repeatable tasks, surface better insights, and test hypotheses quickly

- Designs AI workflows for the team — builds the system, not just uses the tools; models AI-forward behavior

- Runs Omega and Iris across the full portfolio and acts on the patterns they surface

- Decides which AI tools and workflows get adopted, when, and how across the division

- Owns division-level AI quality tradeoffs — where AI accelerates output, and where it must never touch client-facing work unreviewed

- Builds and evolves Power Circuit solutions specific to the division with AI-assisted research; runs a monthly audit to confirm adoption

- Collaborates with the innovation team on enhancements and optimizations that better serve the division's clients

- Consulted on the division P&L and accountable for the profitability of the portfolio

- Forecast the four pillars — Churn, Service Expansion, New Business, Efficiency — in partnership with the MD and VP

- Use the P&L and strategic growth bets to build the business case for headcount and investment; drive efficiency through technology, AI, and process improvement

- Own resolution of every escalation in the direct portfolio

- Partner with Data Intelligence, Media Planning, and Activation teams to keep strategy and execution connected

- Represent Power Digital in market — speaking, content, and client-facing points of view

- Become the internal knowledge hub other leaders turn to for vertical and division expertise

Role Requirements

- Department leadership and management experience required — has led Account Directors or senior marketers as direct reports

- 10+ years of leadership experience in a digital marketing agency, with small business or founder-led client work at the AD level or above

- Experience managing a P&L for profitable growth

- Deep marketing fluency across a high-volume, standardized-service portfolio — foundational packages, repeatable playbooks, and time-to-value; understands where a scaled service model breaks down for an individual account and how to fix it without abandoning the system

- Channel and program strategy expertise across a standardized service catalog — has built or overseen scalable, template-driven marketing programs, not bespoke enterprise strategy, without sacrificing quality

- Measurement expertise: keeping reporting simple, fast, and founder-legible — time-to-value and quick-win ROI — and how to translate marketing performance into terms a first-time marketing buyer can act on, without over-engineering the analysis

- Familiarity with the realities of founder-led decision-making — budget sensitivity tied to personal cash flow, fast decision cycles, and low tolerance for jargon or delay

- Has presented to and pushed back on a founder or owner when the data supported it — can hold a direct, plain-language conversation about performance and expectations without an intermediary layer

- Expertise in contract negotiation, client retention, and client growth

- Proven track record delivering high NPS and retention metrics across a high-volume portfolio

- Extensive knowledge of owned, earned, and paid marketing channels appropriate for small business budgets — content, SEO, paid search, paid social, and programmatic

- Familiarity with Core-specific platforms and tools: standardized reporting and dashboarding tools built for scale, CRM systems, and lightweight marketing automation suited to small business budgets

- Operational discipline — able to run a consistent, efficient system across many accounts rather than reinventing the approach for each one

- Entrepreneurial spirit — energized by building, not just operating; contributes to product and go-to-market strategy, not just client management

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Primary: Meet or exceed a 60% Expansion-to-Churn Ratio (ETCR) on a trailing 3-month average
Secondary Expectations:

- 103% net revenue retention (trailing 6-month average)

- 100% MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue) Growth target achievement (set annually)

- $125K in monthly service expansion pipeline creation across the division

- +90% employee retention rate

- Portfolio NPS at or above 8 (trailing 12 months)

Most Important Things (MITs)

- Division Business & Team Leadership

- New Business & Service Expansion Leadership

- Product Quality, AI & Systems Development

- Client Portfolio Ownership

Benefits & Perks:

- Base salary + commission opportunities

- Robust Medical, Dental, Vision insurance plans with up to 100% employer contribution towards employee monthly premium

- 401(k) plan - 4% employer contribution matching

- Unlimited Time Off available on day one

- Up to 4 hours per quarter for paid Volunteer Time Off (VTO) towards philanthropic endeavors

- Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid

- A one time $100 USD Work From Home (WFH) stipend automatically added to your first paycheck

- Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

- 12 observed United States national holidays + 2 mental health recharge days per year

- Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm

- Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)

- Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance

- Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

Power Digital’s people and culture are at the core of our success, which is why diversity in our team’s backgrounds and experiences are paramount. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Form Health is a virtual obesity medicine clinic delivering physician-led, evidence-based care for obesity and related cardiometabolic conditions. Every Form Health patient works closely with a dedicated multidisciplinary Care Team, including board-certified physicians (many ABOM-certified, and endocrinologists), advanced practice providers, and Registered Dietitians who together deliver comprehensive, one-on-one treatment that includes nutrition, behavioral health, physical activity, and FDA-approved medication, if appropriate. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of clinical care and to treating every individual with empathy and respect.
Founded in 2019, Form Health is a venture-backed, mission-driven company partnering with leading employers and health plans to expand access to high-quality, guideline-based obesity and cardiometabolic care nationwide. remote.title: Senior Security Support Analyst
remote.description:
About us

Coalition is the world's first Active Insurance provider designed to help prevent digital risk before it strikes. Founded in 2017, Coalition combines comprehensive insurance coverage and innovative cybersecurity tools to help businesses manage and mitigate potential cyberattacks.

Opportunities to make an impact with bold thinking are real—and happening daily at Coalition.

About the role

The Senior Security Analyst helps protect Coalition policyholders from cyber loss by assessing security risk, investigating incidents and claims, and translating technical findings into practical recommendations. The role sits within Coalition’s Security team, working across threat intelligence, cyber risk management, and defensive security controls.
This role connects security analysis to business and product execution. In addition to advising customers and security leaders, the analyst partners with Product and internal stakeholders to codify security best practices into underwriting algorithms, rating models, risk-management applications, and internal processes.
Responsibilities

- Assess the security posture of insureds and prospective insureds across programs, technologies, controls, and business environments.

- Investigate incidents and cyber insurance claims to identify root cause, attack vectors, control gaps, and opportunities for prevention.

- Advise customers and security leaders on practical, prioritized improvements across architecture, cloud security, data protection, and compliance.

- Translate threat intelligence and observed attacker behavior into detection tradecraft and actionable security recommendations.

- Partner with Product and cross-functional teams to improve risk models, underwriting approaches, and security-focused applications.

- Track emerging practices, regulatory developments, and industry trends to inform Coalition’s customers, processes, and products.

Ideal Candidate Profile

- Background & Domain

- 2–4 years of experience in security analysis, defensive or blue-team operations, penetration testing, red-team work, incident response, or cyber risk consulting.

- Experience assessing security programs, investigating incidents, or analyzing control effectiveness in complex business environments.

- Exposure to cloud security, security architecture, data protection, threat intelligence, or cyber insurance is particularly relevant.

- Technical & Regulatory

- Strong understanding of network threats, attack vectors, exploitation methods, and intrusion-set tactics, techniques, and procedures.

- Practical knowledge of TCP/IP, network analysis, security technologies, logs, and network traffic captures.

- Familiarity with NIST, ISO, HIPAA, and PCI frameworks, and the ability to connect requirements to real-world controls.

- Collaboration & Influence

- Able to turn ambiguous technical evidence into clear conclusions and prioritized business recommendations.

- Comfortable communicating with security practitioners, business stakeholders, customers, and executive audiences, including CISOs.

- Collaborative and self-directed, with the judgment and initiative expected at the P4 level.

- Effective in a fast-paced, evolving environment where they can help improve processes and products.

Skills and Qualifications

- 2–4 years of experience in security analysis, blue-team or defensive security, penetration testing, red-team operations, incident response, or a related discipline.

- Expert understanding of network threat lifecycles, attack vectors, exploitation methods, and attacker TTPs.

- Knowledge of TCP/IP protocols, network analysis, and network and security applications, including log analysis and network traffic capture analysis.

- Ability to investigate incidents and claims, determine root cause, and recommend effective preventive or detective controls.

- Familiarity with NIST, ISO, HIPAA, and PCI frameworks and their practical application.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide clear recommendations to technical and executive audiences.

Bonus Points

- Experience analyzing cyber insurance claims or translating security findings into underwriting, rating, or risk-scoring inputs.

- Hands-on experience with cloud security, security architecture, data protection, or security control assessments.

- Background in threat intelligence and developing detection tradecraft from observed attacker behavior.

- Experience advising CISOs or customers on prioritizing security improvements based on risk, feasibility, and business context.

- Demonstrated ability to create or improve internal security processes, products, or analytical methodologies.

Compensation

Cisco Security Business Group (SBG) is looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer in a customer-facing role that focuses on technical leadership, two-way advocacy, and expertise across our Security Service Edge (SSE) portfolio.
This role combines deep SWG/SSE, networking and security expertise with the opportunity to influence product direction, solve critically important customer challenges, and serve as the technical link between product, engineering and our most strategic enterprise customers.
Cisco SSE offers a comprehensive end-to-end zero trust access security portfolio including VPN, zero trust access, web inspection in the cloud, firewall as a service, CASB, DLP and more. Cisco SSE deployment flexibility allows customers to select solutions tailored to their needs and transition seamlessly as requirements evolve.
You work globally across regions and time zones in support of our largest and most strategic SSE customers, coordinating with globally distributed engineering teams! Expect participation in a follow-the-sun escalation model and significant travel to customer sites and engineering hubs.
Your Impact
Serve as the technical liaison between Cisco SSE product management and engineering and our largest, most strategic enterprise SSE customers! Represent the product organization to customers by clearly recommending deployment best practices, issue findings, root causes, workarounds, product constraints, and delivery timelines. Represent the customer within the product organization by bringing production context, business impact, operational constraints, and technical requirements into build and prioritization discussions. Own sophisticated escalations, balancing realistic customer expectations with accurate, reproducible technical evidence while advocating for outcomes that protect customer environments. Translate requirements, RCAs, and technical decisions between customer and engineering contexts without losing fidelity on either side.
Key responsibilities:

- Lead the technical relationship on a named set of large and/or strategic SSE accounts, including critical issues end to end.

- Drive proactive account health by improving deployment and rollout planning, configuration and policy consistency.

- Build clean escalations for engineering - timeline, impact, repro, logs, pcaps, redacted configs - and translate outcomes back to the customer.

- Feed recurring customer patterns back into product and engineering roadmaps as concrete requirements.

- Build and support the CX-driven runbooks and documentation from lessons learned and for future SSE deployments.

- Script (Bash/Python) for diagnostics, health checks, automations, and lab reproduction.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field with 10+ years of professional experience in networking, security, or cloud infrastructure; or a Master's degree with 7+ years of experience.

- 7+ years in networking/security with direct customer ownership.

- Experience with DNS, routing, IPsec tunnels, TLS, SAML, SWG/Web Proxy, and cloud networking.

- Experience across zero trust access, VPN, web inspection in the cloud, CASB, DLP, and firewall policy.

- 5+ years of experience with identity and SSO integrations (SAML/OIDC, SCIM) in enterprise deployments.

Preferred Qualifications

- Prior experience handling on-premises and cloud security/networking products in production customer environments.

- Demonstrated ability to influence customer expectations and recommend successful SaaS deployment and adoption strategies.

- Experience supporting large multinational enterprise accounts with global SSE or SASE rollouts.

- Ability to work effectively across time zones and cultures in a distributed engineering organization.

- Coding experience with Bash, Python, or similar.

- Ability to advocate for both viewpoints—customer urgency and engineering feasibility—without distorting either.

- Ability to communicate engineering updates to executive and technical customer audiences, and customer context to engineering.

We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.
Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.
