remote.title: Operations Coordinator
remote.description:
Position Overview
We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented Operations Coordinator to own the job pipeline from intake through invoice — tracking every active job, driving progress at each stage, and making sure nothing sits without action. This role is the operational engine that keeps jobs moving, keeps the team informed, and keeps the insurance process on track.
A significant portion of this role involves direct communication with insurance companies — calling adjusters, following up on claims, tracking appraisal status, and pushing for updates that allow the team to move forward. This is not a passive role. You flag stalled jobs, escalate when needed, and take initiative to get answers without being asked. If you are organized, persistent, and comfortable on the phone with insurance representatives, this role is built for you.
How the Job Pipeline Works
Understanding the full workflow is essential to succeeding in this role:

- A new job comes in — you verify it meets the intake requirements and track it in the system

- You ping the sales representative to confirm the inspection date has been set

- Once the inspection date is confirmed, the job moves to the next stage and a claim number is assigned

- You monitor all active jobs — if a job has been sitting without progress for too long, you bring it to the Operations Manager's attention immediately

- You contact the insurance company by phone and email to obtain required claim documents, following up weekly until received

- Field technicians go out, take photos, and capture data — that data is entered into the platform to generate the inspection report

- You use the report to write the estimate and submit it to the insurance company

- Once submitted, you follow up with the insurance company on the appraisal status — calling and emailing until you have an update

- You communicate appraisal updates clearly to the internal team

- Once approved, the information is sent to invoicing and the job moves forward to completion

Key Responsibilities
Job Intake & Pipeline Tracking

- Receive and log incoming jobs, verifying they meet the required criteria before moving them into the active pipeline

- Track all active jobs through each stage of the process — from intake through inspection, claim submission, appraisal, and invoice

- Maintain an accurate, up-to-date job tracker so the team always knows exactly where each job stands

- Proactively identify jobs that have stalled or been sitting without progress and escalate them to the Operations Manager before delays become problems

Sales Team Coordination

- Ping sales representatives to confirm inspection dates have been scheduled for new incoming jobs

- Follow up consistently until confirmation is received — do not wait for the information to come to you

- Move jobs through the pipeline stages as milestones are hit and document each transition

Insurance Company Communication — High Volume
This is one of the most critical and time-intensive parts of the role.

- Contact insurance companies by phone and email to request and obtain claim documents, adjuster assignments, and claim numbers

- Follow up with insurance representatives weekly — or more frequently when deadlines are approaching — until all required documents and approvals are received

- Track the status of submitted estimates and appraisals, calling the insurance company to check on progress and push for updates

- Communicate clearly and professionally with adjusters — you know how to be persistent without being difficult

- Document all insurance communications including contact names, dates, outcomes, and promised follow-up timelines

Inspection Report & Estimate Support

- Coordinate with field technicians to ensure photo and data capture from job sites is submitted in a timely manner

- Enter field data into the platform to generate the inspection report

- Use the completed inspection report to write the estimate and prepare it for submission to the insurance company

- Ensure all estimate submissions are complete, accurate, and sent to the correct insurance contact

Appraisal Process Management

- Track all submitted estimates through the appraisal process — logging submission dates and expected response windows

- Follow up with the insurance company on the status of submitted appraisals — making calls to confirm receipt, ask for timelines, and request updates

- Provide clear, timely appraisal status updates to the internal team so everyone knows where each job stands

- Once appraisal decisions are received, communicate the outcome and relevant details to the operations and invoicing team so the job can move forward

Invoicing Handoff

- Upon appraisal approval, compile and send the required information to the invoicing team

- Ensure all documentation needed to close the job is organized, complete, and transmitted without delay

Required Qualifications

- Prior experience in operations coordination, claims coordination, or a similar role in construction, restoration, roofing, or insurance-related services

- Comfortable making a high volume of outbound calls to insurance companies, adjusters, and internal team members

- Persistent and proactive by nature — you follow up without being asked and escalate before things become urgent

- Highly organized with the ability to track multiple active jobs at different stages simultaneously without losing detail

- Strong written and verbal communication skills — your phone calls are professional and your documentation is clear

- Reliable in a remote environment with a quiet workspace and high-speed internet

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience working with insurance claims, adjusters, or the property damage restoration process

- Familiarity with construction or restoration job management platforms and reporting tools

- Background in roofing, storm damage restoration, or property insurance claims coordination

- Experience writing estimates or supporting the estimating process in a construction or restoration context

What Makes You a Great Fit

- You look at the job tracker every morning and immediately know what needs to move today — without anyone telling you

- Insurance companies hear from you on a regular, consistent schedule — not whenever you happen to remember

- No job sits in your pipeline without a status, a next action, and a follow-up date

- You escalate stalled jobs before the Operations Manager has to ask about them

- You are the reason jobs move forward — the team counts on you to keep the pipeline flowing from the first call to the final invoice

Requirements
This is a full time role
Up to $6/hr
100% Remote

remote.title: Product & Business Analyst
remote.description:
Launch your product career at Europe's leading music education platform
Matchspace Music is Europe's leading music education platform. We help thousands of music teachers build sustainable careers from teaching, and we are scaling fast across international markets. You will work directly with our VP Product.
This is a role for someone hungry. You want to see how a product is discovered, specified, built, shipped, measured and improved, and you want to be hands-on across the whole cycle. Everything we build follows one cycle: build, measure, learn, repeat. We are looking for a sharp analytical mind that is also creative in solving problems and providing fresh insights. In return you get a front-row seat in building AI-powered platforms, an AI-first way of working, and high visibility to the leadership team as we grow internationally.
Tasks

-
Feature conceptualization. Turn evidence into product ideas. You will run the full loop, from insight, to concept and options, to a sprint-ready story, and back to the data to see whether it worked.

-
Requirements engineering. Turn customer insights and support feedback into clear, buildable user stories with business context, acceptance criteria and edge cases. Own the qualification funnel so nothing rots and no ticket enters a sprint under-specified.

-
Sprint operations. Run backlog hygiene, standup and review mechanics, dependency flags and blocker tracking with our development team, so decisions get made once and stay made.

-
UAT, QA and testing. Own regression and release testing. Reproduce defects properly, keep the bug board honest, and support UAT and end-to-end dry runs.

-
Analytics and performance measurement. Own recurring KPI reporting across our tool stack, close measurement gaps, and turn funnel and cohort data into insight the team acts on. Every feature we ship is measured against the question: did it work? What was the impact?

Requirements

- A relevant degree in business engineering, IT, information systems, digital business administration, or a related field, whether ongoing or recently completed.

- Analytical and creative. You enjoy digging into data to find the real problem, and you are creative about how to solve it. Build-measure-learn is how you already think.

- Structured and detail oriented. You find clean documentation and reproducible analysis satisfying, not tedious.

- Comfortable with data. Excel/Sheets at a solid level, able to read dashboards, willing to learn fast

- Comfortable and confident with software development technicalities, with viewing software code and understanding code with the help of AI

- Proficient in German (min. B2) and English (C1). You can write a requirement someone else can build from. Your main operating language is English. German is essential for our Swiss home market.

- Already using AI tools in your daily productivity workflow and genuinely curious about how software gets built.

- Self-managing in a fast-moving, distributed team.

Nice to have
Agile/Scrum exposure, ticket systems, manual QA or test-case experience, and an interest in music, education or marketplaces.
Benefits

- Work directly with the VP Product in a dynamic, cross-functional team spanning Product, Marketing and Customer Success.

- Full end-to-end exposure: discovery, requirements, delivery, release, measurement and growth.

About the Role
At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an experienced Cloud / Network / Cybersecurity Engineer to support and maintain secure, reliable, and high-performing technology infrastructure.
Depending on your background and specialization, this role may focus on cloud engineering, network infrastructure, cybersecurity, DevOps, systems administration, or a combination of these areas.
You’ll help configure and monitor infrastructure, troubleshoot complex technical issues, manage access and authentication, support security operations, and contribute to infrastructure deployments and upgrades.
This role is ideal for someone who combines strong technical troubleshooting skills with a practical understanding of networking, cloud environments, systems, and security best practices.
What You’ll Own
Cloud & Infrastructure Management

- Configure, monitor, and maintain cloud and infrastructure environments

- Support platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, GCP, or related technologies

- Monitor infrastructure health, availability, and performance

- Assist with infrastructure deployments, upgrades, and configuration changes

- Help maintain reliable and scalable technical environments

Network Engineering & Troubleshooting

- Configure and support network environments

- Troubleshoot network, connectivity, DNS, routing, and infrastructure issues

- Diagnose complex technical problems across systems and environments

- Monitor network health and performance

- Help maintain reliable connectivity across business systems

Cybersecurity & Security Operations

- Implement and maintain security best practices

- Monitor systems for potential security issues

- Support security-related troubleshooting and incident response

- Help identify infrastructure vulnerabilities and operational risks

- Collaborate with relevant teams to improve the organization’s security posture

Identity & Access Management

- Manage user access, permissions, and authentication

- Support appropriate access controls across systems and platforms

- Troubleshoot authentication and authorization issues

- Help maintain secure access practices

- Assist with onboarding, offboarding, and access changes when required

Monitoring & Incident Response

- Monitor systems for performance, availability, and security issues

- Investigate alerts and technical incidents

- Support incident response and troubleshooting

- Identify root causes and help implement corrective actions

- Escalate critical infrastructure or security issues appropriately

Infrastructure Automation

- Identify repetitive infrastructure tasks that can be automated

- Build or support automation for routine technical processes

- Improve consistency and efficiency across infrastructure workflows

- Reduce unnecessary manual administration where possible

Documentation & Technical Operations

- Maintain clear technical documentation

- Document infrastructure configurations, processes, and troubleshooting procedures

- Keep operational and security documentation current

- Support repeatable processes for deployments, incidents, and system changes

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Collaborate with engineering, IT, security, and business teams

- Support technical projects and infrastructure initiatives

- Communicate technical issues clearly to relevant stakeholders

- Help coordinate deployments, upgrades, and operational changes

Requirements

-
3+ years of experience in network engineering, cloud engineering, cybersecurity, DevOps, systems administration, or a related infrastructure role

- Experience with AWS, Microsoft Azure, GCP, and/or enterprise networking technologies

- Strong understanding of networking fundamentals

- Familiarity with cybersecurity concepts and security best practices

- Experience troubleshooting complex technical and connectivity issues

- Understanding of user access, permissions, and authentication

- Experience monitoring infrastructure, networks, or systems

- Strong technical documentation skills

- Strong analytical and problem-solving ability

- Strong communication and collaboration skills

- Professional working English

- Ability to work effectively in a remote environment

Nice to Have

- Relevant technical certifications

- Cloud certifications related to AWS, Azure, or GCP

- Networking or cybersecurity certifications

- Experience with infrastructure or task automation

- Experience supporting incident response

- Experience with identity and access management

- Familiarity with DevOps and deployment workflows

- Experience supporting distributed or cloud-based environments

Tools & Technologies
AWS | Microsoft Azure | Google Cloud Platform (GCP) | Enterprise Networking | Identity & Access Management | Infrastructure Monitoring | Security Tools | DevOps & Automation Technologies
What Makes You a Strong Fit
You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

- Can troubleshoot complex technical problems methodically

- Understand how networks, systems, cloud infrastructure, and security interact

- Think about security as part of everyday infrastructure operations

- Stay calm and organized when responding to technical incidents

- Look for opportunities to automate repetitive work

- Maintain clear documentation rather than relying on tribal knowledge

- Communicate technical issues clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

- Take ownership of problems through resolution

What a Typical Day Looks Like
Your day may include reviewing infrastructure and security alerts, troubleshooting a connectivity issue, managing user permissions, supporting a cloud deployment, or investigating a technical incident.
You may also update infrastructure configurations, automate repetitive tasks, document technical processes, and collaborate with engineering or IT teams on deployments and upgrades.
In short: you help keep the organization’s infrastructure secure, reliable, accessible, and running smoothly.

- Network and system performance

- Speed and effectiveness of technical issue resolution

- Successful infrastructure deployments and upgrades

remote.title: Business Operations Coordinator
remote.description:
We are looking for an experienced, highly organized Business Operations Coordinator to keep the firm running well and to own the operating processes behind our executive team, our partner program and our business development data.
This is not a traditional administrative assistant role. You will support the Managing Partner and other leaders, but you will also own areas of the business end to end. We want someone who notices what needs attention, closes the loop without being reminded, improves recurring processes and puts spare capacity to productive use.
What you will own
Executive scheduling and firm coordination

- Manage calendars for the Managing Partner and other members of leadership, anticipate conflicts and propose solutions.

- Arrange travel, expenses submission and in-person logistics for the Managing Partner and other leaders.

- Coordinate internal, client, prospect and software-partner meetings across multiple calendars, including client calendars when authorized.

- Schedule interviews for candidates advancing through our ATS and make the candidate experience responsive and professional.

- Set up Zoom and Teams meetings, prep sessions and materials. Book in-office days and meeting space through Regus or similar providers.

- Run regular check-ins with leadership, maintain action lists and follow up with owners so commitments do not disappear after a meeting.

Partner program operations

- Maintain the operating record for each software partner agreement: deal registrations, referral submissions, commission and referral revenue tracking, certification requirements and renewal dates.

- Maintain relationship maps of partner sales and alliance contacts, including the accounts and territories each covers.

- Flag to leadership when representatives from different partners are working the same target account.

- Coordinate partner-facing logistics: portal access, co-marketing assets, joint meeting scheduling and follow-up.

Salesforce and business development data

- Own Salesforce data quality: keep account and contact records current, find and fix stale or inconsistent data, and drive the right person to supply missing information.

- Enrich accounts and contacts from conversations, public sources and partner intelligence so that account history and context live in one place.

- Perform account and contact research and build target lists in support of the SDR and leadership.

- Set up and maintain outreach lists and sequences in Mailshake for the SDR and produce simple outreach activity reporting.

- Maintain the firm's purchased and subscribed data sources and recommend additions or corrections.

- Build productive working relationships with executive assistants at clients, prospects and partners.

Onboarding, offboarding and systems

- Own administrative onboarding for new employees and associates: first-month schedule with the manager, introductions, accounts, licenses, access and basic firm information.

- Be the first point of contact for new people during their initial weeks.

- Administer licenses and user access across Google Workspace, Zoom, Lucid, Salesforce, our ATS, Mailshake and other SaaS tools; identify unused licenses; coordinate AWS and Amazon Business account administration with the responsible engineer.

- Maintain the firm's access and credential inventory in the approved password manager, enforce MFA on administrative accounts, and remove access within one business day of a departure or role change.

- Manage Zoom cloud recordings and verify storage and delete redundant copies.

- Maintain naming conventions, folder structures and short written procedures so records can be found by anyone.

LinkedIn, website and external providers

- Publish LinkedIn posts from content supplied by leadership and marketing, and keep the company page consistent and professional.

- Make routine WordPress updates to the website and coordinate larger changes with outside resources.

- Coordinate external marketing, graphics, content and legal providers: hand off assignments clearly, track open work and route completed deliverables to the right person.

Presentations, spreadsheets and meeting support

- Build and format client-ready PowerPoint presentations from content supplied by leadership and subject-matter experts.

- Build and maintain Excel trackers, lists and basic analyses using formulas, filters, lookups and pivot tables.

- Prepare agendas for key internal meetings; attend selected meetings, capture decisions and actions, and file them in the right system.

Continuous improvement and learning

- Continuously evaluate recurring work and implement better ways to do it, including standardization, automation and appropriate use of GenAI tools within the firm's data-handling rules.

- Build working knowledge of the firm's data management and consulting business so that your context and judgment improve over time.

- When core administrative work is under control, move capacity to partner operations, CRM enrichment, research and process improvement without waiting to be asked.

What we are looking for

- Several years of experience in business operations, executive support, professional-services administration, sales operations or a similarly broad coordination role, with a track record of staying long enough in prior roles to take real ownership.

- Demonstrated experience managing complex calendars and follow-up for executives or senior professionals.

- Exceptional organization and attention to detail; high responsiveness; a strong instinct to close the loop.

- A proactive operating style: you identify additional work, risks and improvements rather than wait to be assigned every task.

- Sound judgment about when to act, when to recommend and when a question genuinely needs an answer first.

- High integrity and discretion with confidential company, client, employee, partner and system information.

- A courteous, professional communication style, written and spoken, that sets a constructive tone with colleagues, candidates, clients, partners and providers.

- Solid PowerPoint and Excel skills.

- Experience with Salesforce or another CRM and a real appreciation for data quality and disciplined capture.

- Experience with Google Workspace and comfort learning and administering SaaS tools.

- Effective in a fully remote environment across countries and time zones, collaborating over Zoom, Teams and email.

- Curiosity, an interest in learning the data and consulting space, and a desire to become highly capable with GenAI tools.

- Comfortable with occasional travel or in-person meetings when there is a business reason.

Helpful but not required

- Experience in consulting, professional services, technology, data management, legal, accounting or another client-service environment.

- Experience with ATS, WordPress, Zoom administration, LinkedIn company-page administration, Mailshake or similar tools.

- Experience supporting a software partner or channel program, or coordinating external vendors.

- Experience with prospect and account research.

DataCatalyst is an equal opportunity employer. Employment is contingent on a background check conducted in accordance with applicable law.
What Sets Us Apart
At DataCatalyst, you’re not a cog in a machine—you’re a trusted partner. Our culture is defined by:

- Impact-driven work: Your insights and execution shape client strategy and operational clarity.

Our Story

TopDog Law is not your typical law firm. We're a nationally scaling personal injury firm built for impact and growth — owning the client experience end-to-end, from marketing and intake through litigation. We believe that world-class marketing, paired with exceptional legal talent and operations, creates better experiences and outcomes for clients and the business alike.

Over the past three years, we've grown 2–3x year over year, setting a new standard on the marketing side of the personal injury space and proving what's possible when strategy, speed, and execution align. Now we're applying that same discipline and innovation to firm operations, case management, and national scale — intentionally building the infrastructure, systems, and teams to grow without sacrificing quality, culture, or accountability.

The Opportunity

The Case Manager Lead is responsible for the day-to-day supervision, coordination, and execution of the pre-litigation case management team within the pod. This role ensures cases are properly investigated, documented, and progressed toward demand preparation and settlement.

The Case Manager Lead acts as the operational leader for the case manager team, ensuring case managers execute consistently, maintain organized files, and follow firm workflows and documentation standards. This role partners closely with the Pre-Litigation Attorney, who provides legal direction and strategy for cases.

What You Will Own

1. Case Manager Team Supervision

- Supervise 3–5 Pre-Litigation Case Managers within the pod

- Assign and balance workloads across the team

- Provide guidance on case handling procedures and documentation standards

- Ensure case managers understand priorities and case progression expectations

- Provide coaching and day-to-day support to help case managers execute effectively

- Serve as the primary operational liaison between the case manager team and the Pre-Litigation Attorney

- Handle escalations from clients and providers, resolving issues before they reach the attorney or Ops Manager

- Escalate friction points between case managers and the attorney to the Pre-Lit Case Manager Ops Manager

2. Medical Management & Case Value Ownership

- Own MRI rates, advanced treatment rates, and ensure diagnostics are properly tracked and attended

- Monitor and drive case velocity — ensuring cases move efficiently through each pre-litigation phase

- Ensure settlements meet expected value targets relative to policy limits

- Identify roadblocks to case progression and proactively clear them

- Flag systemic medical management issues to the Pre-Lit Case Manager Ops Manager

3. Case Investigation & Documentation Oversight

- Monitor progress of medical record collection and documentation gathering

- Ensure case files contain required documentation and supporting evidence

- Confirm liability and damages documentation is organized and complete

- Review case files for completeness prior to escalation to the attorney

- Maintain strong case file organization and documentation discipline

4. Data, Reporting & Process Improvement

- Actively use dashboards and reporting tools to evaluate team KPIs and identify underperformance

- Identify process changes and efficiency improvements through direct case experience and data analysis

- Surface operational gaps and improvement ideas to the Pre-Lit Case Manager Ops Manager

- Be comfortable building or pulling reports independently — data literacy is a core expectation of this role, not optional

- Lead onboarding and training for new case managers joining the pod

- Provide informal coaching and identify skill gaps requiring additional training

- Promote consistency in case handling practices and ownership mentality across the team

- Model best practices in case management, documentation, client communication, and ownership through personal caseload performance

6. Personal Caseload Management

- Manage approximately 50 active pre-litigation cases, with an emphasis on higher-value matters

- Be held to a higher performance standard than case managers given the complexity and value of the assigned caseload

- Balance personal case execution responsibilities alongside team supervision duties

- Demonstrate full ownership over cases — regardless of what other departments (medical records, CV specialists, settlement, etc.) have or haven't done, the Case Manager Lead is accountable for outcomes on their cases

- Identify workflow challenges or process gaps through direct case experience and escalate operational improvements when needed

What You Bring

Required:

- 6-8 years of experience supporting Personal Injury pre-litigation matters on cases in multiple states or the state of North Carolina

- Proven experience managing and leading a team of case managers, directing case strategy and workflow to efficiently drive files through each phase and toward timely settlement

- Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail

- Ability to manage a high-volume caseload in a fast-paced environment

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Experience requesting, reviewing, and summarizing medical records and bills

- Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work independently while collaborating with a team

Preferred (Nice to Have):

- Bachelor’s degree or Paralegal Certificate (not required)

- Proven experience managing and developing a team within a legal environment

- Experience in high-volume or fast-growing law firms

- Familiarity with Personal Injury claims processes and insurance procedures

- Experience with case management software (e.g., Filevine, Clio, SmartAdvocate)

- Comfort working in evolving systems and processes

We don't hire on resumes alone. We hire for competence, character, and mindset.

Embrace Change: Open to feedback, embracing change, and always asking "what's next?"

Committed: You care deeply, have your teammates' backs, and show up to build something lasting.

Ownership: You do what you say, follow through, and treat the business like it's yours.

remote.description:
Job Description: Chief Controls Officer (CCO – Controls)
Industry: Banking, Financial Services, Insurance, Investment
Job Type: Full-Time
Reporting To: Chief Risk Officer (CRO) / Chief Financial Officer (CFO) / Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
Job Summary
The Chief Controls Officer (CCO – Controls) is responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing the organization's internal control framework to ensure effective risk mitigation, regulatory compliance, and operational integrity. This role ensures that controls across financial, operational, and compliance processes are robust, consistent, and aligned with organizational risk appetite.
The CCO (Controls) plays a critical role in strengthening governance, preventing control failures, and enhancing transparency across all business functions.
Key Responsibilities
1. Internal Controls Framework
Develop and maintain enterprise-wide internal control frameworks (e.g., COSO)
Ensure controls are effectively designed, documented, and implemented
Standardize control practices across business units
Continuously improve control effectiveness and maturity
2. Control Monitoring & Testing
Oversee control testing, monitoring, and validation processes
Implement continuous control monitoring systems
Identify control gaps and weaknesses
Ensure timely remediation of control deficiencies
3. Risk & Compliance Integration
Align internal controls with enterprise risk management (ERM) frameworks
Collaborate with risk, compliance, and audit teams
Ensure controls support regulatory compliance requirements
Monitor emerging risks and adapt control frameworks accordingly
4. Financial & Operational Controls
Oversee financial controls, including reporting, reconciliation, and revenue controls
Ensure operational controls across processes, systems, and workflows
Strengthen fraud prevention and detection mechanisms
Ensure consistency in control execution
5. Governance & Policy Management
Develop and maintain control-related policies and procedures
Ensure documentation, audit trails, and governance standards are maintained
Support governance committees and reporting requirements
Enhance transparency and accountability
6. Technology & Controls Automation
Leverage technology and automation to enhance control effectiveness
Implement control tools, dashboards, and monitoring systems
Collaborate with IT on system controls and cybersecurity frameworks
Drive digital transformation in control environments
7. Stakeholder Engagement
Provide control insights and reporting to executive leadership and Board
Collaborate with regulators, auditors, and external stakeholders
Support internal and external audits
Promote awareness of control responsibilities across the organization
8. Leadership & Team Management
Lead and develop internal controls and governance teams
Establish performance standards and accountability
Foster a culture of control awareness and discipline
Support talent development and succession planning
Key Requirements
Education
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field
Professional certifications such as CPA, CIA, CISA, or equivalent are highly preferred
Experience
12–18+ years of experience in internal controls, audit, risk, or compliance roles
Proven experience in senior leadership roles (e.g., Chief Controls Officer, Head of Internal Controls)
Strong background in banking, financial services, insurance, or investment sectors
Skills & Competencies
Deep knowledge of internal control frameworks (e.g., COSO)
Strong understanding of risk management and regulatory compliance
Expertise in financial and operational controls
Analytical and problem-solving skills
Leadership and team management
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement
High attention to detail and governance mindset
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Effectiveness of internal control framework
Number and severity of control deficiencies
Timeliness of remediation actions
Compliance with regulatory and audit requirements
Reduction in control failures and operational risks
Audit and regulatory inspection outcomes
Preferred Attributes
Experience in multinational or highly regulated financial institutions
Exposure to IT controls, cybersecurity, and automation tools
Strong collaboration with risk, compliance, and audit functions
Ability to lead enterprise-wide control transformation initiatives
Compensation & Benefits
Competitive executive salary
Performance-based incentives
Executive benefits and allowances

remote.title: Field Applications Scientist – Cell Health
remote.description:
Field Applications Scientist – Cell Health
Beckman Coulter Life Sciences’ mission is to empower those seeking answers to life’s most important scientific and healthcare questions. With a legacy spanning 80+ years, we have long been a trusted partner to our customers, who are working to transform science and healthcare with the next groundbreaking discovery. As part of our team of more than 2,900 associates across 130 countries, you’ll help drive our vision of accelerating answers—and our commitment to excellence.
Beckman Coulter Life Sciences is one of 10 Life Sciences companies of Danaher. Together, we accelerate the discovery, development and delivery of solutions that safeguard and improve human health.
About this role
We are seeking a Field Applications Specialist to serve as the primary scientific and applications expert for our cell analysis and bioprocess analytics portfolio across the Eastern United States. This is a field-based, customer-facing role in which you will be the trusted scientific voice for customers in biopharma, cell line development, and process development—partnering closely with the Sales team while guiding customers to get the most reliable, reproducible results from their workflows.
At its core, this role is about scientific problem-solving. Every customer arrives with a different system—different cell types, different molecules, different objectives—and your job is to understand that system, identify the factors driving variability, and optimize a solution that works for them. Success depends as much on your ability to communicate complex science clearly, to audiences ranging from bench scientists to senior leadership, as on your technical depth. This is a remote role and can be performed from any location within the Eastern U.S. territory.
In this role, you will be responsible for:

-
Serving as the primary applications and scientific resource for customers — Solve challenges and get the most from their instruments and assays, understand the customer’s specific cell types, samples, and goals; diagnosing the many sample- and instrument-level factors that can lead to variable or inconsistent results; and optimizing the workflow to deliver accurate, reproducible outcomes.

-
Supporting antibody and protein quantification applications by understanding customers’ specific molecules—including antibody structure and conformation—and how those characteristics can influence results, then guiding customers toward reliable, optimized measurements.

-
Delivering product demonstrations, on-site trainings, and applications support, both in the field and via web-based platforms.

-
Working cross-functionally as the connective point between the customer and the wider organization: knowing who to engage and when, and collaborating across Sales, Product Management, and R&D to resolve issues and advance opportunities.

-
Capturing Voice of Customer from the field and relaying it to Product Management and R&D, helping to shape future product iterations and ensure the portfolio continues to perform and hold up over time.

The required qualifications for the job include:

-
Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, or a related life science; advanced degree (M.S. or Ph.D.) a plus.

-
Minimum 5 years of relevant life sciences experience in a field applications, technical support, or laboratory/bioprocess environment; a combination of hands-on lab experience with customer-facing experience is ideal.

-
Hands-on mammalian cell culture experience, preferably including fed-batch culture and the maintenance, counting, and viability assessment of mammalian cell lines (e.g., CHO, HEK).

-
Working knowledge of cell counting and viability analysis, including the sample- and instrument-level factors that can drive variability, and the ability to troubleshoot and optimize across diverse cell types.

-
Willingness and ability to travel throughout the Eastern U.S. territory (up to 85%), with a valid driver’s license and the ability to work independently from a home office.

It would be a plus if you also possess:

-
Cell line development (CLD) experience and hands-on familiarity with antibody / monoclonal (IgG) production — highly desired for supporting bioprocess and titer-related applications.

-
An understanding of antibody structure and conformation and how a molecule’s characteristics can affect its quantification and behavior in an assay.

-
Process development or drug manufacturing experience in a biopharma/biotech setting (e.g., upstream/bioreactor, scale-up/scale-down, or GMP environments).

-
Hands-on experience with multimode microplate readers, particularly those with fluorescence polarization (FP) detection capability.

-
Understanding of B2B and QC/QA/R&D customer requirements and of validation processes in the pharma/biopharma industry (e.g., GMP, IQ, OQ).

Travel, Motor Vehicle Record & Physical/Environment Requirements:

- Ability to travel within a defined territory, with an expectation of ~3 days per week in the field engaging customers. This role requires frequent local travel to maximize account coverage and engagement; overnight travel is minimal.

- Must have valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record

remote.title: Head of Originations
remote.description:
About Braavo
Braavo Capital has financed mobile app growth for more than ten years. We’ve deployed billions of dollars to hundreds of app companies through revenue-based products — App Store advance payouts, revenue-based financing, and large credit facilities — underwritten on our own direct integrations with the app stores, ad networks, payment processors, MMPs, and everything in between.
We’re in a phase of rapid expansion, with multiple lines of business and several new product rollouts coming through 2026 and early 2027. We’re hiring for a handful of mission-critical roles to support it, and the Head of Originations is at the top of the list.
The Role
You own origination end to end — from the first conversation to a signed term sheet: building demand in a market that’s still emerging, working out what a company actually needs, negotiating the terms, and carrying the deal through documentation without losing context.
Most capital providers in the mobile ecosystem sell one product and spend their time convincing companies to want it. We don’t. Our range runs from working capital against app store receivables through to large credit facilities, and the job is figuring out which combination fits a company’s economics, timing, and capital structure. It’s a consultative sale rather than a pitch.
You’ll be building this role from the ground up, so there isn’t an established playbook — we need someone entrepreneurial enough to figure things out on the fly. That said, you’ll be working directly with our founder & CEO, so you’ll have the institutional knowledge and experience on hand to learn quickly, adapt, and succeed.
What You’ll Own
Market engagement

- Build and run Braavo’s origination motion — outbound, inbound, referral, event-driven — and own the top-of-funnel number.

- Represent Braavo in the market: industry events, podcasts, social channels, written content, and the private communities where app finance leaders actually talk to each other.

- Build referral relationships that produce recurring flow — agencies, platforms, VCs and venture debt funds whose portfolios need capital they don’t provide, advisors and fractional CFOs.

Diagnosis and structuring

- Run first-pass diligence yourself. Read a company’s revenue, cohorts, payout timing, and cash cycle well enough to know what it can support.

- Match the situation to the right structure — or tell them we’re not it. Saying “not yet” well matters; plenty of those companies are fundable two quarters later.

- Own the term sheet: sizing, pricing, advance rates, thresholds, reporting, exclusivity. Negotiate directly with founders, CFOs, and their counsel.

- Stay on the deal through documentation and close, advocating for it to land while balancing what the customer needs against what we need.

- Bring back what’s costing us deals — pricing, speed, structure, competitor behavior. You’ll be closer to the market than anyone here, and a real voice in what we change.

What Success Looks Like

- Months 1–3. Fluent in our products and the underwriting behind them, with first qualified conversations underway and first term sheets out.

- By month 12. A repeatable origination motion with measurable conversion, multiple closed deals you sourced yourself, and referral relationships producing flow without you pushing each one.

Who We’re Looking For
Someone who can meet a founder or CFO at their level on both halves of the conversation — how their business actually makes money, and how the financing works. That usually comes from equity investing or investment banking in gaming and consumer apps, corporate development at a scaled publisher, an origination seat at a specialty finance or venture debt fund, or growth leadership with real finance depth.
Requirements

- 5+ years in investment banking, equity investing, corporate development, private-credit investing, or a deal-facing business development role — in mobile gaming, consumer apps, or an adjacent sector.

- Fluency in how app businesses make money and where their cash sits: cohorts and payback, subscription versus IAP, app store payout mechanics, working capital cycles.

- Demonstrated deal structuring and negotiation experience. You’ve owned terms, not only relationships.

- A real network among app and game founders, publishers, studio CFOs, and the advisors around them.

It helps if you’ve been on the operator side yourself, or have worked in — or sold against — non-dilutive capital like factoring, revenue-based financing, or venture debt. Prior lending or credit committee experience isn’t required: we’ll teach you the underwriting framework, and we can’t teach market fluency and a network.
Location & Structure
• Based in the United States or Europe. Remote, with regular travel to industry events and client meetings.
• Reports directly to the founder & CEO.
• Base salary plus variable compensation tied to originated and funded volume, and equity participation.
Interested? Send a note and whatever best shows how you think about deals — a memo, a model, something you’ve closed. We read every one.

Every CodePath learner engages our platform, whether they are a college CS student in a direct course, a student at a partner university, an alum sharpening their skills, or a working engineer retraining for the AI era. The Senior Product Manager, Learner Platform Experience owns this platform.

CodePath's courses work because they are intensive, industry-vetted, and human. The hard problem is scale. As we grow from tens of thousands of learners toward millions, the quality and effectiveness of the learner experience on the platform has to improve, not dilute. That demands an AI-First approach: clearly and thoughtfully identifying where AI can accelerate effectiveness, productivity, and scale, and where human connection and touchpoints are essential to maintain motivation, commitment, and progress. The ownership lines are clear. Curriculum owns what we teach. The Learning team owns how it is taught, including the live classroom. Success looks like measurable acceleration in the rate of learning, retention, and engagement, even as the number of students grows by an order of magnitude.

Learning rate is the scoreboard. Plenty of platforms can deliver content at scale. Almost none can prove their students learn faster because of them. You will be measured on outcomes, retention, and engagement, not feature velocity.

The ceiling is enormous. Every course CodePath delivers, direct or through partners, rides on the platform experience you build. As we scale to an order of magnitude of more students, your decisions compound across every learner we will ever serve.

Translate learning, retention, and engagement goals into a prioritized roadmap

remote.description:

We are well-funded, ranked #1 on G2, growing rapidly, and have a people-first culture that is recognized with Great Place To Work® certification and on Fortune magazine's Best Small Workplaces™ List.

Senior Security Engineer

Our Engineering Standards at Karbon:

Balance Speed and Quality

Engineers are expected to balance delivery speed with a strong commitment to quality, meeting agreed timelines while producing reliable, maintainable, and well-tested solutions. Sound judgment in making trade-offs between velocity and long-term sustainability is essential.

Collaborate Effectively

Engineering is collaborative by default. Team members are expected to contribute constructively in design discussions, reviews, and planning, communicate clearly about progress and risks, and support shared team outcomes in both hybrid and distributed environments.

Build and Maintain Systems

Engineers are responsible for building new capabilities while maintaining and improving existing systems. This includes designing scalable solutions, reducing technical debt, supporting operational stability, and contributing to continuous improvement.

Operate with Autonomy

A high degree of autonomy is expected. Given clear objectives, engineers should independently translate problems into actionable technical approaches, proactively identify improvements, and continuously expand relevant technical expertise.

Ownership and Accountability

Ownership is fundamental. Engineers are accountable for the quality, performance, and customer impact of their work from design through post-release support, and are expected to follow through on commitments.

AI-Enabled Engineering

AI is reshaping how software is built, and we are committed to leveraging it as a force multiplier for creativity, impact, and capability. Engineers are expected to confidently apply strong technical fundamentals while embracing AI tools and approaches to enhance productivity, problem-solving, and innovation. Curiosity, adaptability, and enthusiasm for integrating AI into meaningful product development are essential.

Contribute to Team Culture

Engineers contribute positively to a culture of professionalism, transparency, low bureaucracy, and mutual respect, strengthening team performance through authenticity, curiosity, and collaboration.

About the Role!

Seeking a development & cloud focused Senior Security Engineer to join our expanding security team.

The ideal candidate will have passion for AppSec, Cloud and AI. They will be a skilled communicator and relationship builder capable of promoting and building security practices across the organization and into our development processes.

AI is reshaping practices across the board and at Karbon we’re fully committed. We don’t see AI as a replacement but as a force multiplier. We’re looking for Security Engineers who are confident in network & security fundamentals, driven to grow, and excited by the challenges and opportunities AI brings.

What You’ll Own:

- Partner with different areas within Karbon - You will make sure security is embedded from the start from feature design and development to participating in design reviews and threat modelling.

- Balance Security and Delivery - You know how to balance delivery needs with security and can communicate security risks and issues to non technical stakeholders. You understand when it's important to push back, when to compromise and how to work with delivery teams to reach a great outcome.

- You keep up to date on the latest technologies and approaches - You are excited by the new developments such as AI bring to security but also understand the importance of security foundational practices such as good account hygiene, least privilege, attack surface reduction and MFA.

- Identify and assess security risks introduced by AI tools - You’ll assist with reviewing the risks of AI tooling usage & Integration and AI-generated code.

- Apply AI-assisted tooling to accelerate security work - you understand the impact AI can have and utilize it across many areas including triage, threat detection, code review, and documentation.

- Flexibility and confidence to work across multiple security domains - We’re a small team responsible for Security at a fast moving company and you’ll get exposure to many different security domains; you could be assisting with refining and investigating corporate IT security processes in the morning, reviewing a cloud hosted system after lunch and then tweaking detection rules!

- Work effectively as part of a team - Security is a team sport and you understand the need to build relationships and trust across the organization to enhance Karbon’s security posture. You are happy to answer questions and offer advice to teams that will reach out for your assistance.

- Own your work - You take pride in your work, feeling a deep sense of responsibility for the products we develop and ensuring we keep our customers' valuable data secure. This sense of ownership is paramount, and you share this commitment.

- Bring your passion and personality - Your creativity, curiosity, and authentic self make the team stronger. If you've worked in highly political environments, you'll find our culture, free from office politics and valuing openness and authenticity, a refreshing change.

- Help us measure improvement and steer our roadmap - Contribute to Security Metrics so we can track progress and feedback into our roadmap.

What Sets You Apart

4+ years experience in a security or development role across most of the following:

- Collaborating with teams to review designs & implementations for security issues and embedding good security practices across software development

- Triaging issues and reports, assisting teams to remedy items and testing fixes

- Working with external penetration test companies to validate and prioritize findings

- Conducting risk and vulnerability assessments of web applications and APIs and third party suppliers and integrations

- Configuring and tuning SAST, SCA and DAST Tooling

- Working with build/deployment pipelines to incorporate security tooling (Github Actions or Azure Devops YAML based pipelines)

- Assisting with implementing security focused alerting and detections and automations

- Conducting and facilitating organizational & developer focused security training

- Assisting with operational security items such as EDR alerts and MDM

- Contributing to our security roadmap

In addition you’ll need:

- Strong communication skills (spoken and written)

- Some of the following Languages/Frameworks: Microsoft .NET/C#, JavaScript (we use React and EmberJS frameworks and, Python)

- At least one cloud platform: Azure, AWS or GCP (we use Azure predominantly)

- Working knowledge of PowerShell or Bash and Python

- Working knowledge of at least one AI development tool e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Co-Pilot etc

- Portswigger Burp or similar

- Certifications such as Offsec OSCP & AWAE, GIAC, Burp Practitioner, PJPT, Microsoft/AWS development and cloud related are nice to have

- Experience with securing AI applications, systems and AI tooling would be highly regarded

Why Work at Karbon?

- Gain global experience across Australia, New Zealand, UK, and Canada

- Strong benefits package including:

- Flexible Time Off with an encouraged 4 weeks use per year

- Company paid medical for you and eligible spouse/partner and dependents

- Paid dental and vision and eligible spouse/partner and dependents

- 401(k) with company matching

- Flexible Spending Account

- Up to 8 weeks paid parental leave

- Work-from-home stipend

- Work with (and learn from) an experienced, high-performing team

- A collaborative, team-oriented culture that embraces diversity, invests in development and provides consistent feedback

- Be part of a fast-growing company that firmly believes in promoting high performers from within

As we hire across various locations within the USA we are required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role.

The range provided is broad and takes into consideration a wide range of factors that are reviewed when making a hiring decision, such as physical location/cost of living in that location, years of experience, skills, and other business needs.

It is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range and each compensation decision is dependent on each individual case. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which for some roles may include a target bonus, for some roles very competitive equity grant, and very generous benefits. While we believe competitive compensation is a critical aspect of you deciding to join us, we do hope you also spend time considering why our mission, purpose and values are right for you. We are creating something transformational here, and we hope you are as excited about the future as we are!

$131,000—$169,000 USD

Please be aware that Karbon will only contact you via email from our domain, karbonhq.com. If you receive an email from any other domain, please do not click any of those links.

Research has shown that women and underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single criteria. If you've made it this far in the job description but your past experience doesn't perfectly align, we do encourage you to still apply. You could still be the right person for the role!

Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career technologists inside nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions that keep working after the fellow leaves. CodePath is the Employer of Record: we own the full fellow lifecycle, from recruiting and selection through employment, onboarding, benefits, and host support.
Cohort 1 places 100 fellows. The program scales toward 1,000 fellows in year one and 10,000 by year three. This role builds the pod that makes that scale real.

Why this role, now

Claude Corps needs one person accountable for how fellows get hired and how they get employed. Not a strategic HR seat at a distance from the work, and not a recruiting manager who hands off at the offer. A pod lead, running a small team that carries both.

You'll manage the recruiters screening early talent, and you'll manage the fractional HR coordination support that turns an accepted offer into a real employee. Where the program touches the person, you and the Claude Corps program managers work the case together: performance concerns, employee relations, a placement that isn't landing. You bring the process and the employment side. They bring the day-to-day context and the host relationship. Both names are on the outcome.

The math is the other half of the job. We go from 100 fellows to 1,000 to 10,000, and the pod does not grow 100x to match. A team this size clears that volume by building AI into the work: screening support, scheduling, candidate communication, onboarding packets, compliance tracking, the reporting that eats a coordinator's week. We train people to build with AI. We expect the people running our own operations to do the same.
The pod is small in Cohort 1. It grows with the cohorts, and how much it has to grow is partly up to you.

What you will own

Lead the pod. Manage the fractional early-talent recruiters and the HR coordinators supporting Claude Corps. Set the week's priorities, run the load-balancing when a cohort deadline compresses, coach against the bar, and grow the team's headcount and capability as cohorts scale. Fractional support means you are explicit about what you're buying with those hours and what falls to you.

Own screening and selection. Run the funnel from application review through offer, against the program's selection rubric and calibration process. Keep throughput honest: the pod moves volume, and you hold the line on signal quality and candidate experience while it does.

Own the employer-of-record lifecycle. Offers and e-sign, background checks, I-9 and work authorization, payroll setup, benefits enrollment, onboarding. Fellows are CodePath employees, and the experience should feel like it. You direct this work through the fractional coordinators rather than doing all of it yourself.

Use AI to hold the ratio. Find the repetitive work in recruiting and HR ops and get it automated or AI-assisted: resume screening support, interview scheduling, candidate comms, offer and onboarding document generation, multi-state compliance tracking, cohort reporting. Judgment calls stay with humans, and you decide where that line sits. Come with a bias toward trying things, and bring the team along so the whole pod works this way, not just you.

Co-own employee relations and performance with program management. When a fellow's performance or conduct needs attention, you and the program manager run it together. You own documentation, process, consistency, and the employment decisions that follow. The PM owns the host relationship and what's actually happening on the ground. Escalate to the Head of People when the situation warrants it, and know where that line is.

Build the systems. Turn one-cohort processes into repeatable operations: screening workflows, HR SLAs, multi-state compliance, and clean handoffs with our program partners. Bring a point of view on what to standardize and what to leave flexible while the program is still forming

Who you are

- 5+ years across recruiting and HR or people operations, including time owning both, not just one

- You've managed people, and you've managed through others' capacity, including contractors, shared services, or fractional support

- You've run high-volume or early-talent hiring, and you've owned HR operations (payroll, benefits, compliance, onboarding). Employer-of-record, PEO, or multi-state employment experience is a strong plus

- You already use AI in your own work and can point to something you automated or rebuilt with it. Comfort with ATS and HRIS configuration, workflow automation, and prompting is expected, not a bonus

- You've handled employee relations and performance conversations, and you're steady in them

- You're comfortable in a program that is still being built. You bring structure without waiting for someone else to hand it to you

- You hold a high bar on quality and candidate experience at the same time

- You communicate directly and work well across partner organizations with different systems and cultures

- You care about the mission: expanding who gets to build with AI, and doing right by the people you employ

What success looks like

- Each cohort is screened and hired on time, at target size, without cutting corners on signal quality

- The employment lifecycle runs cleanly: offers, onboarding, payroll, and benefits land on time and compliant across every state we hire in

- Cost and hours per fellow hired and onboarded drop cohort over cohort, because the work got automated and not because the team absorbed it

- Performance and ER issues get handled early, documented consistently, and resolved with the program manager rather than around them

- The pod grows in capability and ownership as the program scales, and the fractional support model either scales with it or you make the case for what replaces it

We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

About the Role

Location: Remote, United States

Role-Type: Full-Time, W2 Employee

Reports To: Senior Director, AI Programs

Compensation: $130,000 to $148,000 per year

Start Date: September 21st, ahead of the October 19th cohort launch

Together with Anthropic, CodePath launched Claude Corps in June 2026, a national fellowship program with a $150 million commitment to place 1,000 AI-trained fellows at nonprofits across America. The mentorship model works, but we need experienced professionals to coach and guide those mentors, as well as be responsible for the success of our mentor’s performance and our curriculum delivered to the Fellows. A CodePath Mentor coaches about 20 fellows, so a thousand fellows means more than forty mentors, and someone has to own whether all of them actually deliver. That someone is the Senior Manager of AI Practice.

You manage a team of mentors and you own the delivery outcome for their fellows: at full scale, about ten mentors and 200 fellows, fewer while the program ramps. You are accountable for whether fellows are actually learning, pod by pod and mentor by mentor. When a mentor's pods stall, when a fellow's work drifts off track, when the same problem shows up across three pods at once, it is yours to catch and yours to fix.

Curriculum will be developed, with your influence, at scale, you own the delivery layer: seeing where it lands across your pods and where it doesn't. You keep Commons central to how your mentors and fellows work, and you close the loop back to the curriculum team so the next version is sharper than the last.

This is a hands-on, operational role, and it grows with the program. You start by running the first cohort's small mentor team directly and build the delivery systems that let quality hold as the program climbs from 100 fellows to 1,000. A real part of the craft is reading when a lesson should come from a mentor inside a pod and when the whole group needs to hear it from you in real time. It is built for someone who has run delivery for a team before and would rather raise ten people's game than do all the work themselves.

Key Responsibilities

Manage the mentor team

-
Manage a team of mentors, about ten at full scale and fewer during the ramp: hire, onboard, coach, and hold the bar on the quality of their coaching

-
Run your team's operating cadence: weekly syncs, 1:1s, and the escalation path when a mentor or a fellow needs help

-
Make sure the day-to-day the model depends on actually happens across your team: pull requests reviewed on time, milestone reviews run, host managers engaged

Own delivery for your fellows

-
Own the delivery outcome for your portfolio, roughly 200 fellows at full scale: whether instruction lands, not whether mentors look busy

-
Own the agenda-based instructional time for your whole portfolio: set the agenda, and decide each session whether to teach it yourself, live and to everyone at once, or hand it to your mentors to run in their pods. Either way, whether it lands is on you

-
Hold the quality framework for mentorship: what good coaching looks like, how it gets reviewed, and what happens when it misses the bar

-
Own the milestone-review roll-up across your fellows, and step in on the ones whose work is at risk

-
Replace hand-tracking with delivery systems that hold at volume; the model ran on spreadsheets at 100 fellows and won't at 1,000

Own the CodePath-to-Commons layer

-
Partner with the Claude Corps strategic partners as their counterpart in the field: you see what is landing across your mentors and fellows, and you bring it back as structured signal

-
Own how your team uses Commons: the curriculum ships through the platform, and you own whether it is used the way it was designed

-
Turn what you see in the field into curriculum change requests the curriculum team can act on, and close the loop when they ship

100% of your mentors are running their weekly cadence on schedule and you can pull that from your dashboard, not from what mentors report in standup

-
You can name where each mentor is strong and where they need help, and your weakest spot has a concrete plan implemented within 30 days

-
You've surfaced your top 3-5 delivery patterns across your fellows to the Claude Corps leadership team, and at least 1 has shipped as a curriculum change

You have a single delivery view that shows the state of your portfolio at a glance, in place of whatever was hand-tracked before you

You don't have to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable working with technical and non-technical stakeholders to drive programmatic success

You can hold a room, teaching a live session and keeping it sharp, because some weeks you are the one in front of the group

-
You have owned a delivery or operations outcome at volume, personally on the hook for its quality

-
You have replaced manual, hand-run processes with systems that held up as the work scaled

Strong written communication: feedback, roll-ups, escalations, and change requests, in a remote and mostly asynchronous org

Preferred

You have managed coaches, instructors, or other managers in a bootcamp, fellowship, residency, or other cohort-based program

Comfort with a platform- or LMS-delivered learning model, and reading delivery data to find risk before it surfaces

remote.title: Business Development Representative
remote.description:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. We ship AWS modernization to production in weeks, data platforms migrated, legacy applications and databases refactored, AI agents running against real data, for mid-market and lower-enterprise companies in financial services, healthcare and life sciences, internet and software, manufacturing, and TMEGS.

Our delivery model is built around AI agents that absorb the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, schema mapping, validation, test generation, cutover rehearsal, that traditional consulting bills against human hours. Forward-deployed engineers work on top of those agents, embedded with the customer's team, owning architecture, judgment, and cutover. We commit to a fixed delivery date on a fixed fee. If we slip for reasons inside our control, the cost sits with us.

Most modernization doesn't ship. Ours does. That is the entire pitch.

You'll be the named Mactores contact for AWS sales teams across US territories. AWS account managers, ISMs, partner-development managers, and specialist sellers each carry a partner deck full of firms that all say roughly the same thing. Your job is to make them see Mactores as the agent-native firm in that mix, the one they route to when their customer needs a modernization program finished, not staffed.

What you'll sell maps directly to what AWS reps care about: we're MAP-eligible, AWS Agentic AI Specialized, and predictable on fixed-date engagements. Our founders built the agent platform we deploy, so deployment depth is a structural advantage and AWS reps make money when we win. The conversation starts on the same side of the table.

You won't run deep technical demos, a forward-deployed engineer does that. You set up the meeting, frame the customer's problem, walk through the agent-native approach in business terms, anchor everything in shipped case studies, and hand off to the FDE when the conversation reaches architecture. Then you close the loop: register the opportunity, keep the AWS rep informed, push the deal forward.

This is not a script-and-cadence BDR seat. AWS reps see hundreds of partner BDRs. The ones who get traction can hold a real conversation about the customer's modernization problem, not run through a sequence.

What you will do?

- Build coverage across AWS US sales territories: account managers, ISMs, partner-development managers, and specialist sellers (Data, AI/ML, Modernization).

- Reach out, follow up, show up at AWS Summits and regional partner events, and build named relationships.

- Walk AWS reps through what agent-native AWS modernization means in practice and why it's different from what every other partner in their deck says.

- Anchor every conversation in shipped Mactores case studies: named customer, named baseline, named outcome, time-to-value, cost reduction.

- Identify customer fit, frame the business problem, articulate Mactores' business value, and tee up the technical demo.

- Hand off to the forward-deployed engineer for the architecture walkthrough. Your job is to make sure the FDE walks into a qualified room.

- Source Amazon-originated opportunities into the Mactores pipeline, register them in ACE, and keep the AWS rep in the loop through cycle close.

- Feed market signal back to Mactores leadership, what AWS reps hear from customers, where the partner conversation is shifting, and which messaging lands.

What are we looking for?

- 3–5 years in a BDR, SDR, or partner-development role, with a demonstrated ability to source qualified pipeline from a cold start.

- Comfort talking to AWS field teams. Prior work at an AWS partner, exposure to AWS Partner Central, ACE, or MAP, and time on the floor at AWS Summits or re:Invent are preferred, not required but they shorten the ramp.

- Comfort with the technical concepts of cloud modernization, data platforms, and agentic AI without being the engineer in the room. You can read an architecture diagram, talk through a case study, and name where the customer's pain is. You don't need to debug a Lambda.

- Sharp business-value articulation: you can take a messy customer problem statement, restate it in two sentences, and show how Mactores ships against it.

- A self-managed work style. Remote role, distributed AWS field, no daily stand-up babysitting your activity.

- Travel roughly 30% across the US AWS offices, customer sites, AWS Summits, re:Invent, and regional partner events.

How we work?

We're not selling a roadmap. Our agents run in production today, and our forward-deployed engineers ship with them every day. Mactores is MAP-eligible, AWS Agentic AI Specialized, and holds seven AWS Consulting Competencies and seventeen Service Validations, the credentials that make an AWS rep's routing decision easy.

The agent-native category window is 6–12 months. After that, "agent-native" becomes commodity vocabulary the way "cloud-native" did. We're on the early side of that window, and the BDR who plants the flag in AWS field conversations now will own those relationships when the category gets loud. You'll join an existing partnership and sales motion, the system works. Your job is to add territory coverage and AWS-originated pipeline to it, not invent the function from scratch.

How you'll be measured

A combination of net-new logos and AWS-originated revenue. Not call counts, not email volume, not meetings booked for their own sake. The leading indicator is qualified AWS-sourced pipeline. The lagging indicator is closed-won revenue from customers who came in through the AWS field. Quota structure and targets are discussed in the interview process.

Compensation

Additional Information

We run enablement in layers, from onboarding to an internal community to open office hours to function-specific curriculum we co-develop with each team. This role is the deepest layer, and likely the most important: you sit with a team, build the workflow alongside them, and stay until it holds, which is how AI fluency turns into changed behavior and real impact.

This role may grow to lead a small team of embedded enablement specialists as the function scales.

What You'll Do

- Embed and audit. Rotate through functions. Audit how the team really works, map the repetitive tasks, and find the highest-leverage opportunities

- Build the v1 fast. Develop task-specific agents and automations (research synthesis, status updates, partner reporting, monitoring) using whatever ships fastest: Claude, Claude Code, MCP integrations, and our existing stack including Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, Asana, HubSpot, Zendesk, and internally developed tools. You ship something for feedback in hours

- Productionize and set the quality gates. Default AI output drifts toward mediocrity over time. You turn rough prototypes, yours and your colleagues', into production-grade tools, with the rubrics, evals, and review steps that keep output at a standard the team can trust

- Build reusable assets. Create the skills, plugins, and templates teams self-serve from after your engagement ends, and maintain them as the tools evolve

- Coach to self-sufficiency. The goal of each engagement is a team that no longer needs you. You teach through building alongside people, meet them where they are in their AI proficiency, and leave each team more capable and more confident

- Measure, report, and rotate on. Track outcomes like time saved and quality gained, not platform activity. Present results to leadership to prioritize the next engagement, then document what you built, hand off cleanly, and move to the next function

Requirements

- 5+ years in automation/ops tooling, including recent hands-on LLM/agent work in a professional setting

- Hands-on experience building with LLM tools and low-code/no-code automation platforms (e.g. Claude, n8n, Zapier, Make). Comfortable writing and iterating prompts and evaluating whether AI outputs are reliable enough to hand off to a non-technical team

- A systems thinker who sees a 12-step manual workflow and immediately knows which 8 steps can be automated, and how seemingly disconnected pieces connect

- Ability to embed with non-technical teams, earn trust quickly, and translate pain points into working solutions

- Taste and judgment about quality. You can tell strong AI-assisted work from slop, and you know how to build the guardrails that keep it strong

- Clear written and verbal communication. The range to meet anyone where they are, from a teammate opening Claude for the first time to someone who has been building their own workflows for months, and to move each of them forward

Preferred

- Experience deploying Claude or another enterprise AI assistant across a largely non-technical organization

- Familiarity with MCP integrations and agent architecture patterns

- A background in change management or internal transformation programs

What This Role Is Not

- A software engineer. You will not build infrastructure or ship product code. You automate business processes and build agents that make teams more effective and impactful

- Purely a trainer. You will teach constantly, but you teach through building alongside the teams

- A researcher. You evaluate tools when it serves an engagement, but the core of the job is building, deploying, and iterating

Compensation

CodePath standardizes salaries by level, no matter where you live. Salary within this band is determined by the relevant experience and skills you demonstrate through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a 100% remote position, work from anywhere in the U.S. CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

- Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program

- Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection

- Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 to Jan 2)

- Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support

- Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt

- Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

remote.description:

This is a senior role in our Application & Database Modernization pillar, on a specific mission: leading a large-scale VMware-to-AWS migration and landing it in production. VMware estates are exactly where modernization programs go to stall — sprawling dependency graphs, undocumented workloads, and a hypervisor bill that grows while the migration deck gathers dust. Our customers need that estate moved, cut over, and retired, on a date in the contract.

You'll lead the design and implementation of the target infrastructure: Landing Zones built to AWS best practices, EKS-based container platforms, Infrastructure as Code across the stack with Terraform and CloudFormation, and HA, DR, security, and backup strategies that hold up in production. Aedeon absorbs the discovery, dependency-mapping, and validation grind that would otherwise consume the project's first two quarters. You own the judgment calls, architecture tradeoffs, cutover sequencing, risk decisions and you carry them through to production. You'll also mentor engineers and shape long-term infrastructure strategy with customer stakeholders. If you want your migration experience to end in retired VMware clusters rather than revised project plans, this is the role.

What you will do?

- Lead the design and implementation of infrastructure for a large-scale VMware-to-AWS migration — from discovery through production cutover.

- Architect and build secure, scalable, and highly available AWS environments, including Landing Zones that follow AWS best practices.

- Design and implement containerized application platforms on Amazon EKS; exposure to ECS is a plus.
